articles.title: Black History Month: Sara Misir changed career after fracturing her skull and was first female Caribbean to race for Formula Woman
articles.summary: Sara Misir shares her inspiring journey through motorsport, bouncing back after a serious accident to becoming a professional racer; Race car engineer Jahee Campbell-Brennan reveals his experience in the industry and the work he is doing to increase diversity with the Motorsport UK board
articles.body:
Misir tells Sky Sports News how her career in motorsport racing started. "It has been a long journey. I started when I was four years old, actually in equestrian. And that was my first passion.

"It was my dream to go to the Olympics and I was training to head to the Pan American Games when I was 16-years-old. Unfortunately, I had a small accident, so I had a small change in sports," said the 24-year-old who spoke to Sky Sports News from Silverstone.

She explains the shift from equestrian to motorsport following her tragic accident when she was 16-years-old and how she came back into sport after a recovery that took half a year. "I was training for the Pan American games and me and my horse were warming up one morning.

"We were doing our normal jumping routine, getting ready for competition. And he tripped over a jump and unfortunately, I was half off, so I jumped off and spooked him.

"He spun around and kicked up and I got kicked in the face by my horse. It was about a six-month recovery. I had dislocated my jaw and my skull was cracked in half."

She adds: "It was a traumatic event to get over. And with that, it was a nine-hour surgery. When I got to the hospital, it was an intense way to go from being a top athlete to just being able to make it down the stairs without having to take a break halfway."

The Formula Woman racer says she had her "jaw wired shut" and was on a liquid diet for five months.

Looking to build a career in professional equestrian, she took a step back from the sport after suffering another injury: "About seven months later I got back on the horse, and I started training again. Unfortunately, I got bucked off and broke my shoulder in half that same year."

Misir shares the moment she was introduced to Motorsport racing by her father: "So it was a lot in one year. And my parents looked at me and said, 'Let's just take a small break and just relax from this for a second.'

"So, my dad with a long history in motorsports, introduced me to go-karting, he said: 'Just try this in the meantime it's competitive, high adrenaline, you will love it.'

"And he was right. I instantly fell in love with it. I started go-karting, but it was a love-hate relationship because you imagine I was training horseback riding since four-years-old and I was training that my whole life."

She adds: "I was making podium finishes, traveling around South America representing Jamaica, and then all of a sudden I came into a brand-new sport at 18-years-old with people that have been racing since they were four or five years old that knew it all already.

"But I had a good support network, who were just pushing me to keep on going. And there were so many times that I wanted to quit.

"But, with that village around me, it really allowed me to get to where I am today."

Misir explained the thrill of pursuing a motorsport career: "It's the mental aspect of racing that I love, your head-to-head with people. It's almost like a chess game where you have to pick where to pass, pick how to do it. You have to look at your opponent, see if they're more aggressive and read how they drive.

"I love it because it doesn't matter if you're male or female. I understand that between men and women you have the genetic advantages as a male.

"However, in a race car, it's a mind game. It's more of who has the experience or who can read the track better or who can perform at peak performance and have that mindfulness and relaxation and focus."

Misir reveals the high-intensity impacts that motorsport has not only on your mind but on your body: "People say, 'you just sit in a car and drive.' And it's so much more than that, I've gone a race day where I've lost almost six pounds.

"I went to my nutritionist, and she told me I burned about 9000 calories in one day and that was without going to the gym.

When asked how she balances her work, social and educational life, she said: "Honestly, that has been another big challenge for me because, in January this year I was in school doing my Master's. I had my routine, it was structured. I would go to Jamaica for the three or four races a year for the Jamaican championship and it was very calm.

"Then I went into Formula Woman, and I realised if I want to throw myself into this dream, I have to do it. All or nothing.

"So, I took a year off from school and I left my job and I told them, 'Listen, I'm going for it.'"

Misir is the first Caribbean motorsport driver in her field. She said: "As the first woman from the Caribbean to come out of that, it's been such an honour because I've had such an impression on people.

"When I go back to Jamaica, so many women, kids, and girls come to me and say: 'I want to race too.'"

"And they see that it's possible. Before there was such a stigma and it seemed impossible. And me being able to open the door and show the younger generation that just because it seems impossible it doesn't mean it is."

"If you always do what you can, you'll never be more than you are."

When asked what diversity in the sport is like, Misir said: "It's already such a hard transition to go as a woman into a male-dominated sport and to have to add diversity to that.

"It just makes it such a bigger obstacle. But I'm really hoping to show that it's not as intimidating as it looks. And yes, the racing world is like a shark tank. It can be, but it's nothing that's impossible. If you put your foot down, it will happen.

"I would have to say Lewis Hamilton is doing such an amazing job. I've always found him such a great person to follow behind and follow his steps. I have always admired him for his modesty, respect for others and gratitude and never losing where he has come from."

Misir shares her ambitions for the future. "I would love to get into the GT3 series and get further into my career, but my focus is mainly on the process right now and just working as hard as I can to make sure I'm learning every day," she adds.

"Start making the right decisions, find out what kind of education you need to get there, it's all about just not giving up."

Jahee Campbell-Brennan is a race car engineer who spoke to Sky Sports News about his journey through the industry from working at Ford to creating his own company.

Campbell-Brennan also mentioned some of the barriers when entering his motorsport career. He said: "So when I realised I wanted to have a bit of a turn in my career and head into motorsport there were several barriers, such as some universities being more favoured by the industry.

"There's always that problem where you're only as good as your CV. So having spent some time in the automotive space and then wanting to work in vehicle dynamics and aerodynamics, which is what I specialise in, there was a lot of times where because it wasn't on my CV, even though I'd done lots of training and preparation for myself, I was kind of running into barriers in that sense."

How did he overcome those barriers?: "That is still a work in progress. I'm quite far from where I want to be in the long term.

"So it's just about getting yourself into the right spaces, having the right conversations. Obviously, with engineering you're never going to know everything.

"So, there's a lot of continued professional development, it's just a sort of a process that I think when you're determined enough, you will keep stepping in the right direction."

Having previously worked for Ford, he also faced the challenge of moving from working at a big company to taking on the challenge of creating his own business.

"That was an interesting transition. So, I used to contract there and after about four years, it kind of came to an end.

"For a while before that I'd had some thoughts about wanting to make a change but didn't really know how to do it. So, given my experience and having faced a lot of the barriers that people behind me will continue to face, I've not overcome them all, but I've got a good understanding of them and the best solutions for them."

The Lewis Hamilton Commission report published in 2021 stated: "The case for diversifying motorsport is clear and the time for change is now." After helping to work on this report Campbell-Brennan has put together a framework to identify some of the reasons why there is a lack of diversity in motorsport.

"I'm working with Motorsport UK on their racial diversity committee to consult them on the initiatives that would be effective at that level."

He also told Sky Sports News on the importance of representation: "It is a big thing because if you can see someone who looks like you, sounds like you, thinks like you, it can really inspire you to want to be like them."
authors: Elle-sue Calderbank and Emily Nicole Smith

articles.title: Indy 500: Josef Newgarden claims back-to-back triumphs after final-lap drama
articles.summary: Josef Newgarden secured victory in the 'Greatest Spectacle in Racing' for the second year running after coming out on top in a last-lap battle with Pato O'Ward; the American became the first driver for 22 years to win back-to-back at Indianapolis
articles.body:
Newgarden's victory capped an eventful afternoon at the Brickyard that saw the start delayed by four hours due to severe storms and the race interrupted by multiple cautions.

Yet the drivers managed to get in all 200 laps around the 2.5-mile oval, but only just with the race finishing in the Indiana sunset right before the 8.15pm (1.15am GMT) curfew.

Newgarden gave the crowd of over 300,000 an American winner on the US Memorial Day weekend holiday. Chip Ganassi Racing's Scott Dixon was third.

"I'm just so proud of this team," Newgarden, who took a $440,000 bonus for winning back-to-back Indy 500s, said. "They crushed it - crushed it."

Starting on the front row alongside polesitter Scott McLaughlin and 2018 Indy 500 champion Will Power, Newgarden ran near the front of the pack all day.

But at the end the fight came down to the last-lap shootout with O'Ward, Newgarden sweeping past the Mexican's Arrow McLaren to become just the sixth driver to win back-to-back 500s and the first since Helio Castroneves in 2001 and 2002.

Newgarden's triumph marked team owner Roger Penske's 20th win of the 'Greatest Spectacle in Racing', albeit coming with a whiff of scandal.

Even as Newgarden celebrated chugging from the traditional quart of milk he took a moment to hit back at critics who have labelled him a cheat after his victory at the season-opening IndyCar race in St Petersburg was forfeited for illegal use of the push-to-pass feature that gives drivers a horsepower boost.

An investigation by team owner Penske, who also own the IndyCar series and the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, resulted in Newgarden's disqualification and sanctioning of several officials including the race outfit's president Tim Cindric and race engineer Luke Mason.

"They can say what they want, I don't even care," Newgarden said. "We worked our tails off.

"Luke, Tim, they're not here today but they are a huge part of this."

articles.title: Felix Rosenqvist wins Indy 500 title after thrilling last-gasp overtake
articles.summary: Felix Rosenqvist overtook David Malukas in a dramatic final lap to win the 110th running of the Indianapolis 500 after becoming a new dad earlier this month; watch every F1 race live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Malukas looked like he was in position to win when he passed the race leader Marcus Armstrong off the final restart with one lap to go while Rosenqvist and Armstrong, team-mates with Meyer Shank Racing, fought wheel to wheel down the back straightaway and through the fourth and final turn.

But Rosenqvist had just enough power to pull away from Armstrong and snake behind Malukas before making the decisive outside pass in the final 50 feet.

"What a car. Massive thanks to the team," Rosenqvist said. "We had two cars in the wind at the end and that's a luxury position to be in as a team.

"I felt we had the best car today. In all situations, we kind of had it all under control. That last yellow didn't help us, but it kind of worked out the right way when I got back to third, and then I had a flat-out lap on the high line, and it was just the coolest."

The closest previous finish came in 1992 when Al Unser Jr beat Scott Goodyear across the yard of bricks by 0.043 seconds.

It was Rosenqvist's second career win in 120 IndyCar races and comes after the recent birth of his first child. He is the third Swedish driver to win the race.

"I really miss my wife and my newborn child. I wish they were here," he said.

"I still don't believe it, becoming a dad and winning the 500. Maybe you'll win the 500 and have a baby. It's just unreal. Good job to Marcus and David at the end, they raced really cleanly - and because of those guys you get really good races.

A teary-eyed Malukas said: "I don't know what else we could have done. We were the fastest car in that whole race. We gave it 150 per cent. I almost crashed this car every lap. I'm sewn up with the P2. I don't know what else I can give.

"I give everything to this team, we've had a stellar month and they give me so much support. This place man. We're going to come back again and give it 160 per cent."

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Expect Thunder Call to play a part in Shergar Cup at Ascot live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the Ascot card with the Shergar Cup taking centre stage on Saturday with Ryan Moore, Christophe Lemaire and Yutaka Take all in action; watch all six races live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
Glamorous can have them singing in the Valleys

It's exciting for Welsh trainer Chris Mason to have a runner in this year's Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup and they'll be singing loud in his Monmouth village on Saturday night if All Ways Glamorous takes the opening Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Dash (1.35) at Ascot.

His five-year-old, who will be representing Team Europe, already has a course-and-distance win to his name after impressing off a five-pound lower rating two weeks ago and can give French rider Marie Velon a great experience.

Europe's Bolo Neighs looks poised to get his head in front soon after flashing home in the same race last time but has work to do to turn the tables, while Ryan Moore can be relied upon to get the best out of my old friend Spartan Arrow who has been working well enough to put points on the board for Great Britain and Ireland.

Shrimp Shady is a young horse going places and can give Great Britain and Ireland maximum points in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Stayers (2.10).

Andrew Balding's four-year-old has landed big marathon handicaps at Chester and Newbury already this summer and looks made for this stiff two-mile trip with Ryan Moore set for another plum ride.

Europe, who haven't won the Shergar Cup since back-to-back triumphs in 2013 and 2014, are also well represented with the Ian Williams-trained Hermetic likely to build on his fourth at Newcastle under the classy Christophe Lemaire. This ex-French winner could be well treated off a mark of 81.

It was good to see Richard and Peter Fahey come off the cold list at Southwell on Thursday, just in time for Castle Stuart's run in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Challenge (2.45).

Hong Kong, who are competing as a team for the first time, have a live contender in this reliable four-year-old who has been unfortunate to bump into two Roger Varian improvers at York this summer. South African Luke Ferraris, a well-known name in China, can be relied upon to get the best out of him.

Ian Williams has the services of Irish champion Dylan Browne McMonagle on his likely favourite Night Breeze , a consistent sort who was a good third at Goodwood but needs a career best to win this, which could make him a shade vulnerable. Insanity took this two years ago for Rachel King and can go well again under Europe's Velon.

Thunder a big player for Hong Kong debutant

Thunder Call didn't appear to enjoy Newmarket's undulations last time but can get back to winning ways for the Hong Kong team in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Sprint (3.20).

William Haggas' sprinter won in the style of a very nice horse at York before that and promises to be ideally suited to the stiff finish at Ascot, with British racing debutant Jerry Chau on board.

One to watch out for is Great Britain and Ireland's Cape Ashizuri who is unexposed enough to put a disappointing run in a big field last time behind him. John and Sean Quinn will be happy to have McMonagle in the plate.

Newmarket-based Italian trainer Marco Botti can put maximum points on the scoreboard for Great Britain and Ireland in the Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Classic (3.55).

Archers Bay , another strong chance for Moore, has been bumping into the likes of Ancient Egypt and Heraldry since winning at Newmarket - form that stands out in what doesn't look the strongest renewal.

Team-mate Hoseki is on a roll after rattling up a hat-trick in a course-and-distance fillies' race under a light weight. I'm not sure how much improvement she has left off this five-pound higher mark, though. A more interesting proposition could be Jessie Harrington's Pierre Grosse who is still a maiden but brings solid form to the race in first-time cheekpieces.

The closing Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup Mile (4.30) could determine where the trophy goes this year with Europe's Bullet Point the one I expect to capitalise.

Lemaire partners Haggas' gelding, who has the sheepskins on for the first time after not hitting top stride in two starts this year. He is only a pound higher than when he won a big handicap at York's Ebor Festival 12 months ago.

I also like Rest of the World's Ebt's Guard , a course-and-distance winner who has run well in big handicaps at Royal Ascot and Sandown and looks a big player for Indian ace Suraj Narredu, who won the competition with Team Asia last year.

The Dubai Duty Free Shergar Cup has given me some of my most special days on a racecourse and I'm excited to watch the action unfold in front of what will once again be a big, enthusiastic crowd at Ascot.

I've been lucky enough to ride three winners in the competition including a double three years ago when I was presented with the Alistair Haggis Silver Saddle Trophy for the highest points scorer.

I was on the winning team in 2023 and 2018 and can tell you that lifting that cup is such a buzz. Being part of a team competition is something we don't often experience as jockeys so the rivalry out on the turf on Saturday will be intense.

articles.title: Item surprises big two for Juddmonte International glory
articles.summary: We were treated to another epic renewal of the Juddmonte International on Wednesday but it was far from the match-race that it was built up to be, with Item delivered late to deny Almaqam in a thrilling finish to the York feature.
articles.body:
Hawk Mountain rather unexpectedly set the early pace, with stablemate Constitution River tucked in keenly behind him and odds-on favourite Ombudsman at the rear under William Buick, kept company by another Aidan O'Brien runner, Action.

Hawk Mountain was still in front as they moved to the top of the long Knavesmire straight, with Buick beginning to make headway on the inside rail, as Ryan Moore and Constitution River kicked for home over two furlongs out.

Ombudsman kept making ground on the inside, but the dangers were coming on the outside and it was Ed Walker's Almaqam who pulled away with half a furlong to run, only for Item to arrive in full flight, just getting his head down on the line in the hands of Colin Keane.

Balding has now achieved something his later father, Ian, the trainer of Mill Reef, never managed. He said: "I don't think he had many goes at it, though, in fairness. It's always one of the most important races of the year. So it's lovely to win it with a horse like this.

"We've pitched him in some good races with the belief that he will do well in them, but he's kept improving and improved physically. That's the most important thing.

"He's really a very different horse than the one that ran in the Dante, physically."

He added: "I think anything is possible, he certainly has no problem staying a mile and a half if he wanted to.

"I just want to say a big thank you to the team at home because it wasn't straightforward getting him here. Everything had gone great up until about declaration time and we had a little hiccup there with his feet.

"Thankfully everyone who looks after him have worked overtime to get it right, and happily it was a 5am decision that he got on the box to come up here. I'm very relieved."

On Item's next assignment, the Kingsclere handler said: "I just do not know at this moment in time. I think we've got to sit down and let the dust settle. We've just won a Juddmonte International, that was the plan."

images.caption: Image: Item ridden by Colin Keane on their way to winning the Juddmonte International Stakes

articles.title: Kalpana wins Yorkshire Oaks as gutsy display enough to see off Sparan Nua on day two of Ebor meeting
articles.summary: Kalpana backed up her King George success with another gutsy display to see off the fast-finishing Sparan Nua in a thrilling end to the Thursday feature on the Knavesmire.
articles.body:
Aidan O'Brien's outsider Sugar Island was immediately sent to the front and Ronan Whelan quickly distanced himself from the field, extending the advantage to 20 lengths turning for home.

But as the main players began to eat into that lead, Colin Keane sent Kalpana to give chase over three furlongs out, hitting top gear two furlongs from home, only for Jim Bolger's Sparan Nua - who got a little squeezed at one stage - to make up plenty of ground and close the gap.

The line just came in time for the 10-11 favourite to hold on by a short head, giving Keane, Andrew Balding and owners Juddmonte a second Group One in the space of 24 hours, after Item had landed the showpiece Juddmonte International on Wednesday.

"You knew after going a couple of furlongs it was going to be messy and passing the three (furlong marker) I thought the pacemaker was gone," said Juddmonte's European racing manager Barry Mahon.

"Colin had to commit probably a bit sooner than he wanted. When he saw himself the pacemaker was gone he had to chase her down a little bit, so she was always going to be vulnerable to something closing late, but she's gutsy and knows where the line is.

"She put her head down and got the job done. It's not pretty, but she got the job done and that's the main thing.

"Fast ground, slow ground, 12 furlongs - you wouldn't even be afraid to drop her back to 10. She's just very versatile and the ultimate pro now. She's fully matured now at five years of age and keeps answering all the questions, so it's wonderful."

Connections must now consider how to split their aces, with either Kalpana or Item likely to get a shot at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.

Should Item be given the green light to head for ParisLongchamp, Kalpana - who finished seventh in last year's Arc - will almost certainly bid to win the Qipco British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes at Ascot later in October.

Mahon added: "We have the horse from yesterday too, so whether he'll go to the Arc and we wait for Ascot with this filly - we have to sit down in a week or two and discuss all that, but it's a nice problem to have.

"The horse from yesterday has joined the fray, so we'll decide all those sort of things in the next couple of weeks with the owners and see what they want to do.

"Item is definitely a top of the ground horse. He got away with the good to soft here yesterday. Funnily enough Colin actually said this filly doesn't enjoy the softer ground as much as she did last year, he said she felt like she enjoyed the faster ground in Ascot more the last time than she did today.

"I wouldn't have thought we'd run both in the Arc. Again that will be the owners' decision, but it wouldn't be my first preference.

"I suppose with Item being a colt, if the ground comes up good he'd probably have the preference, and with this filly Ascot was always the target, so it would make sense to sidestep the Arc if the ground is good - but that's a big 'if'.

"She probably will retire at the end of the year. Whether she'll finish at Ascot or if she doesn't go to the Arc whether she'll go to the Breeders' Cup - there's a lot of variables to work out."

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Klassleader looks well treated in the Ebor
articles.summary: William Haggas and Tom Marquand will be hoping Klassleader can regain the winning thread on the final day of York's Ebor Festival; Hollie Doyle believes the son of Lope De Vega can make it two from two on the Knavesmire
articles.body:
If you're willing to forgive his run in the Old Newton Cup at Newmarket last month then Klassleader must be on your shortlist for the £500,000 Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (3.35) at York on Saturday.

My husband Tom (Marquand) felt he simply didn't handle the undulations that day but the way he justified favouritism in a mile and a half handicap at this track back in May gives me the impression he's well treated on a mark of 98.

Alan King's Daiquiri Bay had his moment in the sun in the Copper Horse Stakes at Royal Ascot and looks sure to go well over this extra quarter mile. He's no stranger to The Knavesmire, having finished a gallant third over course and distance in last season's Melrose Stakes, and has been handed a good low draw.

Another open to improvement is the Willie Mullins runner Love Me Tender , a fascinating recruit from Germany who has winning form in soft ground. That said, William Buick's mount has something to prove on his handicap debut over a trip he has never run over.

Zavateri can upset older rivals in Group One feature

I'd love to see Eve Johnson Houghton's Zavateri win the Group One Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (3.00). He's a proven performer at this level and a relatively fresh horse whose run behind Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes was encouraging.

Zavateri was smart enough to win the Group One National Stakes at two, beating Gstaad in yielding ground, and looks a more appealing proposition than Godolphin's brilliant miler Notable Speech .

The faster they go the better for him on his first try over seven furlongs but, although he sets a tough standard on ratings, he has something to prove after disappointing on that much stiffer track at Ascot in the Queen Anne, when he was beaten by Ten Bob Tony . Ed Walker's colt will revel in the conditions and can at least confirm the form.

Japan's classy entire Satono Reve is an interesting contender after his near miss in the Group One Jubilee at Royal Ascot. He tackles this trip for the first time but I'm more concerned about the soft ground for him as he's never encountered conditions so demanding.

Ireland can take the honours in the Group Three Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1.50) at York with the reliable Geryon , who already has winning form at this level.

Ger Lyons's grey landed the Meld Stakes in decisive fashion over this 9f trip at Leopardstown this summer before going down with guns blazing in the Gordon Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Dropping back in distance is very much in his favour and slow ground holds no fears, as he showed when chasing home the classy Hawk Mountain in the Group Two Beresford Stakes as a two-year-old.

Market rival Damysus is another who likes to get his toe in and bumped into one in the Group Two York Stakes last month when he finished behind this week's Juddmonte International hero Item. The addition of cheekpieces could be a plus but he must give seven pounds to my fancy.

It was great to see my husband Tom and William Haggas win the Great Voltigeur on Wednesday with the gorgeous Maltese Cross and I'm hoping they can take another big staying prize with Infraad.

I loved the way he nailed a Class Two handicap at the Goodwood Festival last time, scoring in a manner that suggests he will enjoy the greater test of stamina in the Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (2.25) at York.

A seven-pound rise to 97 shouldn't impede a colt who looks a pattern performer in the making so I can see him getting the better of class dropper Limestone , who is the definitive Group winner in a handicap following his success in the Queen's Vase.

Giving so much weight to progressive types like Infraad demands plenty of Joseph O'Brien's star, though he won't be inconvenienced by the testing conditions - a comment that applies to Andrew Balding's easy ground Newbury winner Mythical Bay .

Air Force One is out to complete a memorable Ebor Festival double in the Sky Bet Constantine Handicap ( 4.10) after winning over the straight track in such game style on Wednesday and looks sure to go well, even with a five-pound penalty.

However, I'm a big fan of Tim Easterby's Red Spells Danger who arrives at The Knavesmire on the back of an impressive win in the Shergar Cup Sprint two weeks ago. He has a six-pound rise to overcome on slower ground but is progressive enough to find the answers.

David O'Meara's Toca Madera was third behind Air Force One on Day Two and also backs up quickly. He's a sprinter in form but just isn't nailing his races and may have to settle for another share of the place money.

Derby runner-up tops bill in Chester Marathon

Godolphin's By The Book and Charlie Johnston's Classic-placed Lazy Griff looks set to fight it out in the Listed Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (2.40) - one of seven races at The Roodee that are live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday.

Championship leader Billy Loughnane partners this Meydan handicap winner who has run well in Group races this year without getting his head in front. He's a solid option but will have to pull out all the stops to deny Lazy Griff .

Charlie's colt was placed in both the English and Irish Derbies last year after finishing just a length and a half behind Epsom hero Lambourn in the Chester Vase. He didn't fire in the Goodwood Cup after making all to win a Listed race at Sandown in July but can prove a tough nut to crack from an attacking draw in stall three.

Drop back in trip no concern for Cracker

George Boughey's exciting Asuka has been dealt a tricky draw in the Class Two Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap (2.05) at Chester on Saturday.

Billy Loughnane will need to ride for luck from out in stall 12 if this smart colt is to complete a hat-trick on ground that will be slower than he's raced on so far.

A better option could be Richard Hughes' five-year-old Whip Cracker who, by contrast, has a much better draw in stall four and ran well at this track back in the spring. Conditions will hold no fears for him on his first try over this kind of trip since his novice win three years ago.

It felt so good to be back on a horse this week - even if it was a mechanical one at Oaksey House in Lambourn!

I had a session on the Equicizer as part of my on-going rehabilitation from the injuries I sustained in that fall at Bath back in May.

The team at Oaksey House continue to be a great support in my fight to regain full fitness, though it's still too early to say when I might be back in the saddle proper.

articles.title: York Ebor Festival: Bacio blazes a trail to win Nunthorpe Stakes as Arapaho Gold takes Gimcrack Stakes honours
articles.summary: Wesley Ward had hit the post with both Acapulco and Lady Aurelia in the past but the Keeneland-based trainer finally got his hands on the Nunthorpe prize as ace sprinter Bacio blazed a trail on the Knavesmire; Arapaho Gold takes Gimcrack Stakes honours at York
articles.body:
While the popular Keeneland-based trainer has enjoyed 13 winners at Royal Ascot, success on the Knavesmire has proved elusive, having saddled Acapulco to finish second in 2015 and come even closer two years later through Lady Aurelia, with Frankie Dettori memorably celebrating passing the post only to find he had actually been beaten a nose by Marsha.

Bacio was the 3/1 favourite to go one better under Juan Hernandez following a brilliant victory in the Palace of Holyroodhouse at the Royal meeting in June and pre-race concerns about the rain-softened ground soon proved unfounded as the three-year-old flew out of the starting stalls.

He had most of his rivals struggling to keep up from halfway and never really looked in any danger of being reeled in, passing the post a length and a quarter clear of Starlust.

No sooner had Hernandez piloted an aeroplane up the York straight he had to run back to the weighing room as he needed to make a sharp exit, with a 6.30pm flight back to America from Heathrow to Los Angeles ahead of the Pacific Classic at Del Mar.

To make sure he made that flight, Hernandez first had to take a helicopter ride from the middle of the Knavesmire to Heathrow and he did not have a minute to spare.

While running back for a brief presentation of the trophies from the Queen, he said: "The horse was giving everything and he'd trained really good.

"He shipped really well, I know a lot of people were worried about the ground for him but he didn't know that.

"He ran great, he broke out of the gate really well, really sharp and he was ready to go. When the gate opened, he was all fire. He was trying to go too early, but I was able to take him back a little bit and save him for the last part.

"He won the race from the gate. Everyone here has done such a great job with the horse. I'm really happy, this race is for America and all my family. Thank you guys!"

Arapaho Gold stretched his unbeaten record to four with victory in the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes.

The Michael Dods-trained gelding won a couple of low-key races at Thirsk either side of being withdrawn after playing up in the stalls at Beverley, since when he had successfully graduated to Listed company in the Rose Bowl at Newbury.

He faced another step up in class for this prestigious Group Two contest, but proved more than up to the task in the hands of Connor Beasley, briefly coming under pressure before getting himself organised and finishing strongly to repel Final Objective by three-quarters of a length at 2/1.

Darlington-based Dods has enjoyed some of the best days of his career at York, having saddled Mecca's Angel to win her second Nunthorpe on this day 10 years ago, while he also sent out the popular sprinter Dakota Gold to win on the Knavesmire six times.

"Once he was out and running I was happy. At halfway he was looking for a bit of room, but once the room came he really quickened up," said Dods.

"Connor just said the last 100 yards he gave him some feel the way he quickened away from them. He's a good horse, this was a big step up and he's taken everything in his stride. When we've wanted him to step up he has and he has stepped up again there. He's just some horse isn't he?"

On future plans, Dods added: "He'll go to the Mill Reef (at Newbury) now and that will probably be it for the season and we'll see where we go next year.

"He's got the speed for six furlongs as you've just seen and I don't think you'll see any problems getting seven. He quickens up and he gallops. It's an interesting problem (planning), but we'll deal with it. He's an exciting horse to have and it's brilliant that we've got him in the yard.

"We've had a lot of luck at York, but this is right up there with the two Mecca's Angel wins and winning that is unbelievable."

Richard Brown, racing advisor to Wathnan Racing, who own the runner-up Final Objective, said: "It was a massive run, it's one where you are delighted because the horse has run a huge race.

"A furlong out I thought he was coming to win, he hasn't been straightforward and Hamad (Al Jehani) has done a great job training this horse and that is a career best, so we'll keep him busy.

"He wandered about when he won at Thirsk last week and he has done again, so I think we'll pop a pair of cheekpieces on.

"There's a race in France, the Prix Eclipse, that we could look at, but we'll all have a sit down and see what might be best for him."

Adrian Keatley said of the third home, Hell Of A Spin: "He's a hardy little horse who tries his heart out and he's running consistently well in these good races.

"You'd like to think there's a nice one in him one of these days, I don't think the trip or ground were a concern for him, it was just the winner quickened away.

"He's been placed in a Molecomb and Gimcrack now. There could be a race in France towards the back-end for him - we'll keep trying."

Image: Arapaho Gold, ridden by Connor Beasley, on their way to winning the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack at York

articles.title: Kevin Blake's Ebor Festival tips: Sky Sports Racing expert looks ahead to day four at York with three selections
articles.summary: Day four of the York Ebor Festival takes place on Saturday and is headlined by the Sky Bet Ebor Handicap; Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake has put up three selections on the card on the Knavesmire
articles.body:
York have been unlucky with the weather this week, and the softening ground has created some extra challenges, but all being well we can hopefully finish the week on a high.

The Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1:50) is the first race of interest, and one that looks overpriced is the Hamad Al Jehani-trained Archivist . Long-term readers may recall that I put him up as my selection in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and while it didn't work out for him on the day, he gained compensation on his very next start when overcoming what was considered a near impossible draw of 20 in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood.

Not only did he overcome his draw, he did it with a bit to spare and that performance signalled his readiness to be competitive at stakes level. This course and distance should suit him well and any ease in the ground shouldn't be overly inconvenient for him. He is drawn a little wider than ideal, but that is bearable given his price is so big. A big run from him wouldn't at all surprise.

The Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (4:10) is another extremely tough sprint handicap, but I'm game to have a swing at the Andrew Balding-trained Dance In The Storm . The manner in which the betting markets have been so positive about her in her four starts this season has strongly suggested that she is considered better than a handicapper.

While she has won two of her four starts over seven furlongs this season, she has very much been shaping as though she is worth a try at this shorter trip. She has a career-high mark to overcome, but this different distance could well unlock notable further improvement. She is a really interesting contender and warrants support.

The final selection of the week comes in the concluding Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (5:20), and it is the Ger Lyons-trained Diego El Queso . The four-year-old has a progressive profile, winning a handicap at Leopardstown in good style back in April prior to having an absence of 12 weeks that suggests he may have had a hold up.

He returned to action with a tremendous run to finish second to Thread Of Gold in a valuable handicap back at Leopardstown and that form has been well advertised by the winner since then. He was well fancied for a similar race to this at Glorious Goodwood, but the race went wrong for him, yet he still managed to catch the eye in finishing sixth.

He is capable of better than he was able to show there and with both this course and distance and the ease in the ground all promising to suit him, he can be expected to make a bold bid for compensation.

images.caption: Image: Kevin Blake provides his latest Ebor Festival tips

articles.title: York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby
articles.summary: Charlie Appleby's Notable Speech returned to top form when rocketing to victory in the City Of York Stakes under William Buick, setting up a potential return to America for the Breeders' Cup Mile.
articles.body:
Charlie Appleby's chestnut has been a top-class performer for the last three seasons, with his big-race haul including the 2000 Guineas and Sussex Stakes in 2024, the Woodbine Mile and Breeders' Cup Mile in 2025 and the Lockinge at Newbury this spring.

He suffered a rare blip when only sixth as favourite the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot in June, but dropped back to seven furlongs on the Knavesmire - albeit on easier ground than ideal - and showed his true colours in the hands of regular partner William Buick, travelling powerfully before quickening two and three-quarter lengths clear of the chasing pack as the 9-4 favourite.

Appleby said: "You've got to admire him. You get good horses who can do it at two and three, but when they do it at four and five you've got to doff your cap to them.

"We're allowed to give these horses the opportunity to do it and that is full credit to His Highness Sheikh Mohammed and Team Godolphin for letting us keep these horses in training, as it would be very easy to retire a horse like him.

"The likes of Modern Games and Space Blues, they could have gone to stud much earlier. It was different with Rebel's Romance as a gelding, but if I had a mare I'd be the first person to send one to a horse winning Group Ones at three, four and five.

"This new seven-furlong Group One is what we needed in the UK and it is being well supported. A horse like him winning it will hopefully give the race plenty of kudos."

The Moulton Paddocks handler will now target a second Breeders' Cup success with his charge, adding: "I spoke to a couple of guys from the Breeders' Cup earlier today. What is good about today is he has showed his versatility on ground slightly softer than ideal.

"Going to Keeneland you can have a question mark about whether the ground will be a bit more autumnal, so hopefully that has given us the confidence that we can head straight to the Breeders' Cup now."

Infraad to swerve Leger despite impressive Melrose win

William Haggas was lukewarm on a tilt at the Betfred St Leger with Infraad after he continued his progression with victory in the Sky Bet Melrose Handicap at York.

The Ghaiyyath colt had made steady improvement during his five-race career so far, most recently scoring a mile and a half at Glorious Goodwood.

He stepped up to a mile and three-quarters for a prestigious £180,000 contest Haggas has won three times before and was a 100-30 joint-favourite under Tom Marquand, alongside Joseph O'Brien's Limestone.

The two market leaders were both in contention racing inside the final furlong, but it was Infraad who saw out the extended distance best, coming home two lengths clear of the staying-on Galilean Quality, with Limestone fading into fifth.

"He's improving but he's quite raw. He was a bit juvenile before the race and a bit edgy, so he's still got a bit to learn," Haggas said of the winner.

"Tom did say he's pretty relentless when he gets going and he won comfortably."

Bookmakers cut the winner to 8-1 from 16-1 for the St Leger at Doncaster next month, but Haggas feels the season's final Classic may be too much too soon for a horse he views as more of a long-term project.

"We won this race a few years ago with a Highclere horse called Guaranteel. He won by three and a half lengths off top-weight and we ran him in the Leger, but it came too quick for him," the trainer continued.

"I suspect, without speaking to connections, that the Leger will come too soon in this horse's career too, and it's more likely he'll go for the Noel Murless at Ascot.

"I don't like putting a gun to their heads too early, especially a big raw horse who I hope will be a nice horse for a few years, so let's not squeeze the lemon dry too early.

"I think he's going to develop, he's only just getting the hang of it and that's his first time at this distance, so hopefully he'll develop into a Cup horse."

images.caption: Image: William Buick aboard Notable Speech
Image: Tom Marquand takes the acclaim of the crowd aboard Infraad

articles.title: York: Daiquiri Bay fends off rivals to land thrilling Ebor on the Knavesmire
articles.summary: The Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay denied the Wathnan Racing-owned Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling crescendo to the Ebor Handicap at York
articles.body:
While the four-year-old has always been a smart handicapper for Alan King, he has taken his game to another level since being gelded during the off-season, with a comeback win at Newmarket followed by his narrow verdict in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal meeting in June.

King had opted to keep his powder dry for the £500,000 feature of the Ebor Festival since and was rewarded in some style, with Rossa Ryan burying his mount in midfield for much of the one-mile-six-furlong journey before making his move shortly after the home turn.

Daiquiri Bay moved stylishly into contention and with the near side rail to help, dug deep in the closing stages to get the better of the Wathnan Racing-owned pair of Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling three-way finish.

King said: "It was a great ride from Rossa and I'm just blown away.

"We still have plenty of hurdlers and he'd make a nice one, but I don't think I'll suggest that today!

"This has been the plan since Ascot, after that Rossa said to put him away for the Ebor as he had a tough race. He broke the track record at Ascot, so we were able to give him a little break and build him up.

"His preparation has gone great, the rain came and I almost think he's a better horse on slow ground."

He added: "It's a very special day. We had the favourite back in 2003 with Salsalino, but he only finished third. It's a very special race.

"We came hopeful he'd run well and he was always in the right place, but I thought the Wathnan horses were coming to do me.

"He was entitled to do what he did and he was still on the up, so we hoped. Horses we've brought here before have been more exposed. We actually needed him to go up after Ascot so he was guaranteed a run.

"When you win these big races it is always emotional and we don't win as many as we used to.

"I've always tried to win an Ebor but you need one on the way up and this one was."

When asked if he would now consider the Melbourne Cup King laughed: "I don't travel, you do well to get me to go to York!"

Wathnan Racing's adviser Richard Brown was proud of the second and third, with Hopewell Rock a possible runner in Australia's most famous race in November.

Brown said: "It's one of those where you are delighted that they have run so well but you want to win - all credit to Alan King because his horse was so brave.

"I thought we were definitely getting there with Hopewell Rock, but they've run brilliantly.

"The Melbourne Cup reps are here and I still need to find out if he qualifies for it, but that was the plan.

"Opportunity has not been an easy horse; he's actually been quite difficult so William (Haggas) and his team have done a brilliant job with him.

"He might be a Cup horse next year, we'll see. He'll get better with age."

images.caption: Image: Daiquiri Bay and Rossa Ryan won the 2026 Ebor

articles.title: Deauville: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record with Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet win
articles.summary: Aventure produced an upset in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet, defeating the previously-unbeaten Diamond Necklace in the Deauville Group One; also on the card, Senorita Bonita dazzled for the Simon and Ed Crisford team in the Prix Morny
articles.body:
Aidan O'Brien's daughter of St Mark's Basilica was expected to dazzle once again in France, as she had done when landing the Prix Marcel Boussac, Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches and Prix de Diane on her travels during what was an unbeaten six-race career to date.

However, she had no answer to the experience of her Christophe Ferland-trained elder, who added to last year's Group One strike in the Prix Vermeille.

In a close-up third was the Charlie Johnston-trained Timeforshowcasing, who ran a big race in the hands of Jack Mitchell.

Pierre-Yves Bureau, racing manager for owners the Wertheimer brothers, said: "We're very happy and when she won the Prix Corrida earlier this year we were very happy but then made a mistake by running over a mile and a half in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud.

"There was a strong field of fillies including Diamond Necklace, but what our mare did is just wonderful, she is such a champion. We will be very happy to have her as a broodmare one day, but we will enjoy her racing for the moment!"

Second to Bluestocking in the 2024 Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Aventure earned a quote of 20/1 for this year's renewal by Paddy Power following her triumph over O'Brien's star performer in the hands of Maxime Guyon.

However, there will be no third attempt at Europe's richest middle-distance prize for the five-year-old who will instead remain at 10 furlongs for the Prix de l'Opera post the main event on Arc day before a possible trip to Keeneland.

Bureau added: "It's quite unusual, but this filly is getting more speed with age and 10 furlongs is her perfect trip now. She has been really well prepared for this race.

"The plan is to run her in the Prix de l'Opera and then if everything goes well we might take her to the Breeders' Cup for the Filly & Mare Turf, but we will take it step-by-step and one race at a time. The next step will be the Prix de l'Opera."

Senorita Bonita proves jet-propelled in Prix Morny

Senorita Bonita demonstrated her devastating turn of foot to scorch to Sumbe Prix Morny glory.

The 900,000 guineas top lot from April's Craven Breeze-Up sale, Simon and Ed Crisford's filly arrived on the Normandy coast looking to follow up her victory in Newmarket's Duchess of Cambridge Stakes, a win that received a timely boost by Lowther Stakes scorer Libertango earlier this week.

Held up towards the rear by Oisin Murphy, with Clive Cox's Royal Ascot winner Orthodox ahead, the daughter of Starspangledbanner had plenty of ground to make up on Aidan O'Brien's front-running Carry The Flag entering the final third of the contest.

However, once the champion jockey stepped on the accelerator the response was instant, as not only did Senorita Bonita rapidly eat away at the deficit but then surged readily clear of the long-time pace-setter for a thoroughly impressive victory.

Simon Crisford said: "She's shown a great turn of front and obviously they set some very good fractions up front but she finished off super well - she galloped out strongly.

"She was a little bit slow out of the gates and behind the bridle early, but they were going quick and the race set up for the closers and she was the best of the closers.

"At halfway I briefly thought we might have a mountain to climb here, but she's got such a good turn of foot that at the furlong pole you could see she was going to come home strong."

It was the father and son training team's second victory in the Group One race after Vandeek in 2023, while it continues the fine record of fillies in the contest following on from Venetian Sun's triumph for Karl Burke 12 months ago.

The Victorious Racing-owned Senorita Bonita will now go in search of further top honours in Newmarket's Cheveley Park Stakes and was made 5/2 by bookmakers for a race where she could meet former foe Libertango once again, as well as another recent York winner, Sun Goddess.

"All roads lead to the Cheveley Park now at the end of September and that was a fantastic performance," continued Crisford.

"It was a deep, deep renewal and it was a really, really pleasing effort and she's looked really impressive there.

"Any Group One is fantastic to win and we are all just delighted. It's a great testament to the staff back at home and everyone involved and it's great to win for Shaikh Nasser (bin Hamed Al Khalifa) and Shaikh Khalid (bin Hamed Al Khalifa)."

images.caption: Image: Aventure claimed the honours at Deauville (photo:Zuzanna Lupa)
Image: Winning rider Oisin Murphy with Senorita Bonita

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Marquand and Haggas can claim August Stakes success
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle gives her verdict on the action from Windsor, Goodwood and Sandown, providing her take on the August Stakes, Celebration Stakes and Solario Stakes.
articles.body:
The feature race on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday evening is the Listed Weatherbys August Stakes (6.30) which can go to my husband Tom Marquand and trainer William Haggas.

They combine with the reliable Tenability who has winning form at the track and won't mind any rain, as he proved at Ascot last autumn when he chased home Al Qareem in the Cumberland Lodge.

Tenability has been kept fresh since beating popular stable companion Hamish at Goodwood in June and then finishing third in a Group Three in Deauville over further than this trip.

He brings more compelling recent form to the race than the intriguing Silawi , who has been disappointing given what he achieved in winning the Group One International in Canada last October and then chasing home Opera Ballo in the Jebel Hatta in Dubai in January.

The most prestigious race of the day on Saturday is the Group Two Virgin Bet Celebration Mile Stakes (3.10) at Goodwood and I won't be forsaking the likeable Zavateri , who has a great chance to gain his first win of the year.

Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old, who is eased in grade, ran respectably behind Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes at this track and wasn't disgraced in Notable Speech's Group One at York last weekend.

This is a quick turnaround for a colt who has winning Pattern form at this track in the Vintage Stakes but I take him to win an ordinary renewal at the probable expense of Qirat , last year's shock Sussex Stakes winner who will be a danger to all if he gets loose on the front end.

George Scott must have been tempted to pitch Forty Years On into Stakes company so it's interesting he sets out to exploit an appealing mark in the Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Handicap (2.00) at Goodwood.

This progressive filly, who has been raised 8lb to a rating of 96, made it four from five with a winning reappearance in easy ground at Newbury in early June so any further rain on the South Coast will be a positive.

She's up against Andrew Balding's Ghost Mode , who won at the Goodwood Festival despite hanging badly. He's up four-pound for that and looks her biggest threat, though The Fingal Raven has the form in the book to go well at a much bigger price.

William Haggas's Too Darn Hot gelding High Degree looks capable of giving his rivals weight in the Virgin Bet A Good Bet Handicap (2.35) at Goodwood.

Cieren Fallon's mount was galvanised by first-time cheekpieces at Pontefract a couple of weeks ago and remains lightly enough raced to cope with a four-pound rise.

I do think Gary and Josh Moore's Too Soon looks well handicapped despite winning at Epsom back in early summer and he can give young Warren Fentiman a good ride if he's fully wound up for this return from a three-month break.

I love to see Welsh trainer Chris Mason's All Ways Glamorous run well, just as he did in the Shergar Cup, but he may have to settle for a share of the minor money in the Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap (4.55) at Goodwood.

My preference is for David O'Meara's Toca Madera who ran a big race in defeat at York last week before struggling to make an impact in softer ground there four days later.

He is better judged on his staying on fifth in the Stewards' Cup at this track - a performance that suggests he can take the measure of some battle-hardened rivals in the capable hands of Danny Tudhope in this tough finale.

I'm expecting Secret Of Life to keep her unbeaten record intact in the Group Three BetMGM Atalanta Stakes (2.50) at Sandown on Saturday.

Ralph Beckett's daughter of Pinatubo took the Listed Coral Distaff on Eclipse Day and looks ready for this step up in class in receipt of weight from some classy older fillies.

I'm also keen on Calendar Girl who was a Listed winner on her reappearance at Haydock Park three weeks ago. Like Secret Of Life, she's got an entry in the Group One Sun Chariot so Owen Burrows will be hoping for another step forward.

Both of Sonic Angel 's wins have been achieved ion the All-Weather but Simon and Ed Crisford's colt has the credentials to make a successful turf debut in the Group Three BetMGM Solario Stakes (3.30) at Sandown on Saturday.

I liked the way Oisin Murphy's mount drew clear of the 90-rated Siouxperb on debut at Newcastle before following up under a penalty at Kempton Park this month.

Of course, this demands much more but entries in the Group Two Champagne Stakes and the Group One Dewhurst suggest this son of Dark Angel has a bright future. He can take the measure of Godolphin's promising Yarmouth debut winner Rock Montreal .

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft .

articles.title: Constitution Hill set for serious test at Kempton on Saturday
articles.summary: The September Stakes is set to pose a very different question of Constitution Hill with top-class rivals Gethin, Bay City Roller and Tornado Alert all set to face Nicky Henderson's star
articles.body:
Nicky Henderson's former superstar hurdler is two from two since switching to the level, but the Group Three contest at the Sunbury track represents a major step up.

The nine-year-old has been ridden by Oisin Murphy and Ryan Moore so far in his new adventure, but Loughnane's name appeared alongside the Seven Barrows runner for the weekend on the British Horseracing Authority administration site.

Loughnane's agent Tony Hind, who also represents Moore, confirmed the switch saying that Henderson was happy for the championship-leading jockey to take over on Michael Buckley's pride and joy.

"His first choice was Ryan who is riding in America," he said. "So I offered him Billy who is definitely there riding in the Sirenia Stakes and Nicky confirmed this morning he was fine for Billy to ride."

Leading the opposition is George Scott's runaway Coronation Cup winner Bay City Roller as he prepares for the Arc, while Saeed bin Suroor has entered the Group One-winning Tornado Alert, booking Murphy for the ride, and the evergreen Dubai Future.

Last year's Great Voltigeur winner Pride Of Arras represents Ralph Beckett, with the Owen Burrows-trained Gethin and Joseph O'Brien's Small Fry other smart performers among the 14 possibles for the mile-and-a-half feature.

Gethin disappointed when last seen contesting the Coral-Eclipse at Sandown in early July, but Burrows is hopeful he will show his true colours this weekend ahead of a potential tilt at the Arc.

Callum Rodriguez, who has steered the Wathnan Racing-owned grey to each of his three career victories to date, is set to return to the saddle, with James Doyle likely to be required to ride for the Wathnan team in the Sprint Cup at Haydock on the same afternoon.

Burrows told Sky Sports Racing: "He's in good shape. Callum had a sit on him last Wednesday because we thought James would be up at Haydock for the Sprint Cup and he was very happy with him.

"It's been a bit frustrating we've had to sit on him during the hot months, but we knew we had no issues worrying about weather for this race and I'm looking forward to getting him back out.

"He was fine after the Eclipse. If you look at the sectionals it was pretty hard for the first four furlongs and quickish ground as well, hence why we didn't want to go again on it."

On the prospect of taking on Constitution Hill, Burrows added: "He obviously brings a nice dimension to the race and I'm sure it will add plenty on the gate, but like any trainer I just want to beat all the opposition, so if he's in it then he's included in that.

"It will be interesting, but I'm hopeful. Wathnan bought him with an Arc in mind, so if Saturday went well I dare say that will be his next step."

images.caption: Image: Ryan Moore was drafted in to ride Constitution Hill at Kempton in place of the suspended Oisin Murphy

articles.title: Galopin Des Champs: Two-time Cheltenham Gold Cup winner dies aged 10 following accident in field
articles.summary: The 2023 and 2024 winner of the Cheltenham Gold Cup, Galopin Des Champs has tragically died following an accident in a field; The 10-year-old horse, who was trained by Willie Mullins, was found with a severe injury on his near front leg.
articles.body:
Ruby Walsh revealed the news late on Tuesday evening that the 10-year-old gelding had suffered an injury to his near front leg which vets concluded was irreparable.

"Sadly Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved," Walsh said in a statement to Racing TV .

"He was checked a few times throughout the morning but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg.

"He was attended to by our vets immediately but X-rays revealed extensive unrepairable damage."

Walsh paid tribute to a horse that won not only two Gold Cups at the Festival but three Irish Gold Cups at Leopardstown.

The statement continued: "He was a fabulous racehorse whose short time with us has left lots of broken hearts but none more so than those of Greg, Audrey and Sarah Turley and Adam Connolly who looked after him for so long. He will be sadly missed."

images.caption: Image: Galopin Des Champs has tragically died at the age of 10

articles.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Ascot, Kempton and Haydock preview as Almeraq headlines Sprint Cup field for husband Tom Marquand
articles.summary: Royal Ascot hero Almeraq looks the one to beat in the Sprint Cup at Haydock on Saturday; Constitution Hill takes on his toughest test in the Group 3 September Stakes at Kempton, facing Gethin, Tornado Alert and Pride Of Arras
articles.body:
ALMERAQ is on a retrieval mission after flopping in the July Cup, but he can clinch his second Group 1 of the season in the Betfair Sprint Cup (3.40) at Haydock Park on Saturday.

A combination of the fast ground on an undulating track may have been his downfall at Newmarket, but my husband Tom [Marquand] reports his mount fresh and well for an assignment he should relish.

Shadwell's colt came of age in the Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee Stakes at Royal Ascot and has proven form on soft ground, which I expect will bring the best out of him.

Clive Cox's Coppull looked a colt going places when stepping up to seven furlongs to win the Hungerford Stakes at Newbury and arrives at Haydock in rude health. He's a Group 1 winner in waiting but he's never encountered soft ground before which will raise a question mark if he takes his chance.

The step up to seven furlongs is ideal for another William Haggas horse, THUNDER CALL , who reappears in the Schweppes Handicap (1.40) at Ascot on Saturday.

He was doing his best work in the closing stages of the Shergar Cup Sprint at this track last month and remains well enough treated off 93 to capitalise under Cieren Fallon.

I also respect the chances of Michael Dods' gelding Northern Express who loves this track and is only 2lbs higher than when scoring over seven furlongs at York two starts ago. I certainly don't think he's making the long trip from Darlington for no good reason.

Heyzoom has been gelded since finishing a creditable fourth to St Leger fancy Enceladus in the King George V Stakes at the Royal Meeting and looks sure to go well in the Tote.co.uk Money Back 2nd Handicap (2.10) at Ascot.

However, Owen Burrows' three-year-old comes up against a formidable opponent in DECADE OF TIME who has been in great form this year and has been crying out for the step up to this 12-furlong trip.

Since winning his novice, Jack Channon's colt has produced two solid runs in 10-furlong handicaps at Newmarket and Goodwood. He won't be troubled if the rain comes, either.

At a bigger price, Andrew Balding's improving Kameko colt Cape Fear streaked away from his rivals at Windsor 12 days ago and can make an impact if this race hasn't come too soon.

The quicker they go the better for reliable sprinter HAVANA BLUE who should get the race run to suit in the Club 26 Handicap (4.35) at Ascot.

Julie Camacho's gelding gained reward for a string of seconds when getting his head in front on the July Course at Newmarket last time and remains well handicapped off a mark of 85.

I'm also prepared to forgive Fast Track Harry a disappointing run in the Great St Wilfrid at Ripon last month. He's better judged on his second to Amazing Journey over this course and distance in July while rain would be welcome for northern raider Golden Mind who is well handicapped on last year's slow ground form.

West Acre has become very disappointing but continues to fall down the weights so it would be nice to see him show that old sparkle off a mark of 99 in the closing Tote.co.uk For Racing & Sports Betting Handicap (5.10) at Ascot.

My idea of the winner, though, is Ed Bethell's filly FLUORESCENCE whose beating of Badri at Pontefract was paid a compliment when that horse made the frame in the Listed Beverley Bullet.

The daughter of Twilight Son ran well in Listed company in the summer so her new mark of 97 shouldn't prove prohibitive in this ordinary handicap, especially if the ground is on the fast side of good.

Classy Gethin to capitalise on ease in grade

The highlight of the afternoon at Kempton Park on Saturday is the William Hill September Stakes (2.50) which looks a good opportunity for the classy GETHIN to get back to winning ways.

Owen Burrows' colt has taken on the likes of Ombudsman and Constitution River since winning a Listed race on the Polytrack earlier this year so should find this less taxing.

Godolphin's Tornado Alert was a Group 1 winner in Germany last year and isn't to be underestimated. He should sharpen up for his close fourth in the highest company there last time while Pride Of Arras is a danger to all if he can build on his great effort behind Item in the York Stakes.

That brings me to Constitution Hill , who will have his fan club out in force for this steep step up in grade. This will be a searching test of his capabilities on the Flat against hardened stakes horses, but I hope he can keep the dream alive with a bold performance.

articles.title: Kempton: Constitution Hill tastes Flat defeat as Pride Of Arras takes September Stakes
articles.summary: Former champion hurdler Constitution Hill tasted defeat for the first time on the Flat when only managing fourth in the September Stakes at Kempton; The race was won by 2025 Dante Stakes winner Pride Of Arras, who defeated odds-on favourite Gethin.
articles.body:
So brilliant at his peak in his hurdling days, Nicky Henderson's superstar has remained one of racing's biggest draws since switching to the level - but this Group Three affair was a major step up from his victories at Southwell and at this track in February and March respectively.

As the odds-on Gethin took early command of the mile-and-a-half contest, Billy Loughnane and Constitution Hill (9-2) sat in a close-up fourth and were still travelling with a degree of menace turning for home.

Asked for his effort just outside the two-furlong pole, there was only a flattering moment of hope before it became clear he was not going to get involved and instead it was the Ralph Beckett-trained Pride Of Arras (11-2) who swept to the front, holding off the rallying Gethin by a length.

Constitution Hill had arrived at Kempton with the Melbourne Cup a tantalising option for the autumn, but Henderson will now return to the drawing board and said: "Melbourne is gone now sadly. Today was always going to tell us what we were going to do next and I suppose he's posing us another question now.

"I don't think we want to go under a mile and a half, that is for sure, and 12, 13 or 14 furlongs seems to be the range of where we go with him. I do think he is going to come on for the run, what with the way he got there as if it was going to happen, but from a furlong out I think he took a bit of a blow. It will sharpen him up.

"He's going to be eligible to run in handicaps now and it will be interesting to see what the reaction on Tuesday is. It could allow him into some very lucrative handicaps in England, Ireland or wherever you like.

"From two novice stakes of very differing strength and depth it was a big step today and we'll now just wait to see what it does for his mark."

He added: "We'll find a nice race for him somewhere and he's by no means finished yet, I can promise you that."

Australian dreams may have been crushed for Constitution Hill, but for connections of the winner Pride Of Arras, a trip to Canada is now on the cards as last year's Dante and Great Voltigeur scorer showed his class on the Sunbury synthetics.

Beckett said: "He's a good horse and was good in the Dante and Voltigeur last year and a talented individual.

"He had a really bad foot problem that came to light just before the John Porter and he wasn't really ready when he ran against Calandagan in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, but I had to run him somewhere.

"I then thought he lugged out when second (to Item) in the York Stakes and was still thinking about his foot.

"I thought he looked a million dollars before the International and hadn't looked better. It was a great disappointment to all of us we couldn't run at York. They loaded him at York before all the other horses had gone behind and I'd say he was looking at the horses walking towards him and that's what set him off

"I thought today he would probably find the surface a touch deeper than he would like so you could probably upgrade it a little bit.

"I think there is a good chance he will really enjoy Toronto when we take him to the Canadian International."

On the impact of Constitution Hill at Kempton, Beckett added: "It's great that the crowds have come out and we're in the entertainment business, but inevitably you have to worry about your own horse.

"I'm delighted there is a crowd and it was a good race. The first two are good horses and Constitution Hill wasn't disgraced."

articles.title: Friendly Soul makes all to strike in Prix Vermeille
articles.summary: Friendly Soul delivered a breathtaking performance in the Prix Vermeille, kicking clear from some way out and lasting out gamely for a second Group One success.
articles.body:
A top-level winner in the Prix de l'Opera on Arc weekend two years ago, John and Thady Gosden's five-year-old missed the entirety of last season through injury.

However, she has slowly come to the boil in three starts this term, most recently chasing home Diamond Necklace in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

And although she was tackling a mile and a half for the first time on her return to France, jockey James Doyle did not appear to have any stamina doubts, sending his mount straight to the lead from the off.

Friendly Soul and Composing had built up a healthy lead over the chasing pack rounding the home turn and while both Pink Panthera and Sunly came from further back to mount a late challenge - with the latter perhaps an unlucky loser after missing the break and encountering traffic problems in the straight - the Gosden runner had enough in hand to claim victory.

"It was a hugely sporting decision from her owners, George and Julia Strawbridge, to keep her in training at this age," Thady Gosden told Sky Sports Racing.

"Last time she was here she won the Prix de l'Opera, a couple of years ago now. She likes to do things her own way and took James to the front there, but she didn't get an easy lead at all - she got attacked in the false straight there and was never really able to get a breather.

"Obviously she's a hugely talented filly and very tough too. It's great to have her back to her best."

Friendly Soul is a 16-1 shot for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with Coral. When asked whether Europe's premier middle-distance contest could now be on the agenda, Gosden added: "It was obviously her first time over a mile and a half, so it was slightly unknown territory before this.

"I haven't had a chance to speak to George and Julia yet, we'll see how she comes out of the race and see where they'd like to go with her, but of course it's great to have it (Arc) as an option."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli driving for Mercedes rather than Ferrari has taken pressure off Italian says Karun Chandhok
articles.summary: On the latest episode of Sky Sports F1's The F1 Show, Simon Lazenby, Karun Chandhok and David Croft discuss Kimi Antonelli's stunning win at Monza; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year.

He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old.

His father, Marco Antonelli, has previously revealed he held discussions with Ferrari but the Scuderia did not want to sign someone so young whereas Mercedes were willing to take the risk.

On the latest episode of The F1 Show, Chandhok said: "I actually think by not making him a Ferrari junior, not putting him in front of Ferrari, not trying to make him a Ferrari young driver, and going down the Mercedes path, is actually the best thing that Marco Antonelli has done for his son. It's taken the pressure off in so many ways.

"Could you imagine if he was there as a Ferrari Italian driver? The pressure would be unbelievable. And Mercedes have done a fantastic job of nurturing him and bringing him here.

"I saw Kimi's parents and his sister afterwards by the Mercedes motorhome. They looked so delighted with the fact that obviously he'd won the home Grand Prix. I couldn't help but think they've managed to take away some pressure by not having him as a Ferrari driver."

Last week, Antonelli played down suggestions that he could drive for Ferrari in the future as he claimed he could spend his entire career with Mercedes.

He said "as much as Ferrari is massive, incredible brand, I am very happy where I am" but Chandhok hopes he does drive in red one day.

"For the sake of the sport and the sake of Ferrari, I hope, a bit like Lewis, in 10, 15 years' time when Kimi's achieved a whole lot of things, maybe he will become a Ferrari driver. It'll be great for Ferrari to have him one day," he said.

Antonelli has stunned most of the F1 paddock this year with his speed and performances so far, but his most recent in Monza where he won from 19th on the grid made headlines around the world.

Sky Sports F1 's David Croft says Antonelli is a "generational talent" but is still "keeping his feet on the ground".

"At the start of the weekend he was getting pranked in the paddock, getting cream pies flung at him from his team as they got him back with a birthday surprise. I'm not sure the majority of F1 drivers on the grid would have stood for that," said Croft.

"Kimi absolutely revelled in it and there is a driver who is so at ease and so comfortable in the team that he's in. Long may that continue on track and off it as well. He is a total breath of fresh air for Formula 1."

Chandhok added: "He's been prepared from a much younger age as a professional, all-rounded driver - how to work with a team, how to work with a bigger structure.

"These kids now who are being signed to driver programmes from the ages of 10, 11, 12 in junior karting, they're being moulded from a younger age.

"You compare and contrast to the generation above, a Fernando Alonso or a Michael Schumacher, they only signed to professional contracts by the time they were already in F3.

"So I think, in some ways, it's not a surprise, I guess, that he is arriving as a more finished package because he's had 10 years of being as part of a professional structure, which the generation above wasn't."
