articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Owen Burrows’ filly can claim Park Hill success
articles.summary: Our ambassador previews a busy Thursday on Town Moor which features the Group Two Park Hill Stakes – live on Sky Sports Racing from 1.15pm
articles.body:
The race they call the Fillies' Leger, the Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes (3.00), is one of the highlights of the opening day of the Betfred St Leger Festival at Doncaster on Thursday and I expect a competitive renewal to go the way of the Owen Burrows-trained Waardah .

She has run two big races in a light campaign in pattern company this year, including in the Group Two Lillie Langtry Stakes at the Qatar Goodwood Festival, only to pay the price for a touch of freshness early in the race - her first since May.

With a hood fitted for the first time, she can prove too good for some classy types including Fairy Glen who shone out in Meydan in the spring when taking the Dubai Gold Cup over two miles from Friday's probable Doncaster Cup favourite Caballo De Mar.

Simon and Ed Crisford's mare has proven form on the back of a break so shouldn't be troubled by a four-month absence and her stamina beyond this extended mile-and-three-quarter trip is assured.

Godolphin's filly Musical Times brings a burgeoning reputation to the other Group Two on the opening day at Doncaster, the Betfred May Hill Stakes (3.35) for the two-year-olds.

Unbeaten in novice races at Newmarket and Yarmouth and on course for a possible crack at the Group One Fillies' Mile, this exciting daughter of Lope De Vega is a fascinating runner in this recognised Classic trial.

However, she hasn't beaten a lot at this stage so I'm taking her on with Irish raider Sea Of Rain , who has already proven herself at a high level with victory in a Group Three at the Curragh last time. Jim Bolger's filly has plenty of experience and won't mind a bit of cut in the ground.

Can't see past Vegas in valuable sales race

I just can't see past the likely favourite Night In Vegas in the big juvenile cavalry charge on the opening day, the Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes (1.50).

Eve Johnson Houghton's colt boasts a lofty rating of 102 yet gets a considerable amount of weight from many of his closest rivals under the terms of this race. His credentials are impeccable with a valuable auction race success at Newmarket last time coming on the back of a creditable third in the Group Two Richmond Stakes at the Goodwood Festival.

I'm hoping to see my husband Tom (Marquand) go well on William Haggas's God Given Talent who was unlucky in running when fourth in a hot nursery at York's Ebor Festival on his first start for the yards since leaving James Ferguson.

Satellite Of Love , who like God Given Talent has a rating of 91, can also play a part. Clive Cox's colt was unbeaten in his first two starts before finishing a well beaten fifth behind the thrown-in Group One winner Sun Goddess in that York sales race.

Cox filly can make winning nursery debut

Art Of Life is yet to get her head in front but can make a winning debut out of novice company in the British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap (1.15) on Thursday.

Cox's filly has been unlucky to bump into a couple of promising types at Newbury, including when a shade too keen behind Tom's hot favourite Sweetwonderfulyou last time.

I marginally prefer her to Richard Spencer's likely favourite Speed Of Sound , a lovely Sioux Nation filly who ran a stormer at the weights behind Sun Goddess in that valuable sales race at York.

At a much bigger price, Richard Hannon's Rollthedicebaby has the talent to get back on track off an easing mark after finishing in the pack behind Speed Of Sound on the Knavesmire.

Tom and his boss William have the one they all have to beat in the mile and a quarter Pertemps Network Handicap (2.25) on the opening day.

King Of Earth impressed me when taking a valuable Curragh handicap in the summer in first time cheekpieces and can be forgiven his effort last time in Group Three company at York.

Back in a handicap with the ground and a good draw in his favour, he can get quickly back on track at the possible expense of John and Thady Gosden's Runman .

It's early days for the son of Frankel who put a two-month break behind him to win over this trip at Newbury last time. He looks very well treated off just a three-pound higher mark and will enjoy conditions on Town Moor.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

articles.title: St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runner-by-runner guide
articles.summary: With the 250th instalment of the world's oldest Classic on the horizon, Sky Sports Racing's Mike Cattermole runs through every contender going to post on Town Moor at 3.35pm on Saturday; Watch the race live from Doncaster on Sky Sports Racing.
articles.body:
So, who will take Saturday's special renewal of the Betfred St Leger? First of all, it's great to see the Derby winner, Christmas Day, lining up. Not all that many do the double, a fact that I appreciated early in my racing life when even the mighty Shergar could manage only fourth. In more recent years, Camelot just missed out on his Triple Crown attempt.

Remember, the Leger is only a furlong and a half shorter than two miles but you still need speed as well as stamina to take it.

Never Say Die, St Paddy, Nijinksy and Reference Point are the last four to have backed up here after Epsom, however, so good luck to Christmas Day.

He is closely matched with stablemate Pierre Bonnard but Aidan O'Brien's hopes of a tenth Leger may be challenged by his own son, Joseph, trainer of the favourite, Enceladus.

Jockey: Sean Levey | Trainer: Aidan O'Brien

I feel rather sorry for Action who, being a close relative of last year's Derby winner and Leger fourth Lambourn, did little wrong in a juvenile campaign which yielded a third to Bow Echo in the Royal Lodge Stakes and then an even better second to Hawk Mountain here in the Group 1 Futurity.

Even this year's campaign didn't start too badly when he improved on a fourth in the Sandown Classic Trial to chase home the future Juddmonte hero, Item, in the Dante at York.

It all started to go wrong when he raced way too freely in first-time cheekpieces in the Derby and since then he has been sacrificed as a pacemaker in the Irish Derby, King George and the Juddmonte. In the last-named, he didn't get away anywhere quickly enough to do his job and a mid-race move still ended with him being tailed off.

It doesn't augur well for his prospects as he steps up in trip here.

I think he needs an arm around his powerful shoulders!

Many who watched this year's Derby may have gone away thinking that Alderman might end up being aimed at the Leger after he finished off rather well to take fifth (would have been fourth in another stride or two) behind Christmas Day, some two and a half lengths in front of Rebel Rocker in sixth.

Note that Pierre Bonnard, Ancient Egypt and Item were among those behind him.

However, he failed to build on that in the Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket, notably on firm going, when last of the five runners.

He remains a five-race maiden, albeit a talented one, and on the evidence of Epsom when the Derby was run on soft ground, any rain that falls this week will be a bonus.

Even then, he has way too much to do here.

After last year's Derby winner Lambourn failed to follow up here in fourth, we still await the first to emulate Reference Point who remains the last to win both Derby and St Leger in 1987.

Christmas Day has a bright chance of doing it, though, especially if showers arrive on Town Moor. His Derby win on soft ground was pretty emphatic, beating Arc-bound Maltese Cross by nearly three lengths and that is about the best form on offer here.

He failed to back-up in the Irish Derby but went down fighting behind Benvenuto Cellini and a neck in front of Pierre Bonnard. The form-line with his stablemate was replicated in the Great Voltigeur when Pierre Bonnard reversed the placings in receipt of 5lb from the Derby winner as they were left toiling behind the upwardly mobile Maltese Cross.

Christmas Day has been a model of consistency all season and shapes as though he could just about stay the trip. I doubt he will improve for it, however, but he should be bang there.

This big, long-striding colt is unbeaten as a three-year-old and gets better every time he shows up. The form of his King George V Handicap win at Royal Ascot has received multiple boosts and he did his bit in style to land the Group 3 Gordon Stakes at Goodwood next time.

There was a lot to like about the way he settled the issue with a fine turn of speed approaching the final furlong there, albeit with a tendency to edge right again, and rather more pronounced than it was at Ascot. Maybe that is why they have fitted cheekpieces for today.

It is six years since Joseph O'Brien won his first Leger with Galileo Chrome and, with this vintage season yielding so much, he must be optimistic of following up with this son of Sea The Stars.

The fact that his half-brother won at a mile and six furlongs must add to the expectation, plus the fact that he arrives here fresher than most and with the chance of improvement to come.

Sadly, Dylan Brown McMonagle is still recovering from a horror fall at Bellewstown and so Billy Loughnane is booked to wear the iconic Niarchos family silks.

Looked one to follow for Andrew Balding when winning his maiden at Chester's Boodles May Festival and was expected to take some beating in the Queen's Vase, for which he started favourite. But he could manage only sixth to Limestone.

His very decent second in the Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket was a step back in the right direction but then came a heavy defeat in the Great Voltigeur at York. Sure, he probably did too much in that race, but it is hard to see him turning that all around here, even with the newly fitted cheekpieces.

One of the more unexposed runners, winning two of his four starts, including a tight verdict over Del Maro in the Listed Cocked Hat Stakes at Goodwood.

However, his progress stalled in the King Edward VII Stakes at Royal Ascot when he was way too keen and was left behind in the home straight.

His full brother Arabian Force stays a mile and six but he needs to settle down a bit to emulate him and also needs to improve a lot.

A record of one win from six but he is steadily improving and gained his only win with a comfortable stroll here over a mile and a half in July.

He backed that up with a clear second in a valuable handicap at Goodwood but, as the lowest rated in the line-up, he does have a lot to find with some of these and even then, is not guaranteed to last out the trip.

That said, he has been quietly backed in recent days and looks the first string from a top stable enjoying one of its finest campaigns.

Stablemate of Enceladus and looks the second string but is, without doubt, the most fascinating contender in the field.

He has had an incredible turnaround after showing precious little in his first three starts, ranging between six and a half furlongs and a mile. Then, on his fourth appearance, and an SP of 250-1, there was more than a glimmer at Naas, again over a mile. It was some eyecatcher!

Plenty more were watching when he then stepped up to almost a mile and a half at Killarney and duly strolled home by nine lengths. Next, he went off at 22-1 and landed the Listed Vinnie Roe Stakes over a mile and six furlongs at Leopardstown, hitting the line strongly, again with his customary high head carriage.

So, we know he stays the trip and probably has more to offer and will be ridden by Saffie Osborne. Could they make history together? Anything is possible but in truth he needs to find plenty more to steal this.

The most experienced runner in the field who looked every inch a Leger type at two when landing the Group 3 Zetland Stakes at Newmarket and Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud (beating the smart A Boy Named Susie) both over a mile and a quarter. The former was on good to firm and the latter on a testing surface so the ground comes alike to him, clearly.

Had a patchy first half of the season, including when only seventh in the Derby, but has done a whole lot better in his two most recent appearances.

He stayed on well for third, a neck behind Christmas Day, in the Irish Derby and then, in receipt of 5lb from his Derby-winning stablemate, reversed the form in the Great Voltigeur, giving Maltese Cross something to think about until the last few yards.

I cannot have this Camelot colt failing for stamina, especially as his dam's half-sister was third in the Park Hill, and he has the form in the book to go very close.

A useful and relatively unexposed colt who probably has more to offer but was a well-held sixth in the Derby and ran to a similar level in the Geoffrey Freer at Newbury.

There is stamina on his dam's side that suggests he will stay well but even so, this represents a very tough ask.

The only filly in the line-up who won the Listed Cheshire Oaks but has come up short in Group company since, including in the Epsom and Curragh Oaks.

She didn't seem to quite get home in the Lillie Langtry Stakes at Goodwood over a mile and six furlongs two starts back, which was a surprise as she is bred to be suited by a trip like this one. At least she shaped better in the Give Thanks Stakes back over a mile and a half at Cork last time.

Needs to find something from somewhere and I wish her well as she is named after a personal heroine of mine, who also happens to be a distant relative of my American wife!

ENCELADUS arrives here on the crest of a wave for Joseph O'Brien, who has enjoyed a marvellous season. He is on an upward curve with improvement not guaranteed, but surely very likely, and with the promise that the trip will suit.

He gets a narrow vote and could become the first European Classic winner for the Niarchos family since Study Of Man won the French Derby in 2018. It would be the second Classic of the season for Billy Loughnane.

Derby winner Christmas Day has performed at a consistent level all season but his prep at York perhaps lacked a little sparkle and I wouldn't be at all surprised if Pierre Bonnard finished ahead of him again, especially over this trip. Both are by Camelot (as is Amelia Earhart) who is a real stamina influence.

I will be intrigued to see how Highwayman goes and fancy him to grab fourth in a race that the incredible O'Brien family look set to dominate.

articles.title: Doncaster: Waardah impresses with Park Hill Fillies' Stakes win
articles.summary: The Owen Burrows-trained Waardah took top honours in the feature Park Hill Fillies' Stakes on the opening day of Doncaster's St Leger Festival, with Callum Rodriguez in the saddle.
articles.body:
Sporting a hood for the first time in a race, she was more tractable for Callum Rodriguez and she added another Group Two win to her record having landed the Lillie Langtry at Goodwood last season.

The heatwave has hampered her progress this summer as she prefers some cut in the ground and when third in the same Goodwood event last month, that was just her second start of the season.

Sir Mark Prescott's Consent made a bold bid from the front, but Waardah (5-2) wore her down and pulled a length and three-quarters clear of the staying on Danielle.

Burrows is now eyeing a possible bid for a Group One double, with the Prix de Royallieu on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp and Champions Day at Ascot both on his radar.

"I'm pleased the hood was on because she jumped a little bit too well. She wears it at home because she's not easy and the team at home do a good job keeping a lid on her," he said.

"She got into a nice rhythm and two furlongs out I was happy.

"She's in the race in France and if that went well and Ascot turned up soft and she was well, I wouldn't be afraid to back her up.

"She's had a quiet year because the ground hasn't been in her favour at all and I can imagine she'll be heading to the breeding shed after (this season)."

Rodriguez added: "That was very good, delighted with that. She's promised that all year and with a bit of cut in the ground today we could see her to best effect.

"She likes that ground and stays very well. The race unfolded perfectly for her as there was a nice, even tempo, the track suited with the long straight and she stays well.

"She was strong through the line, it was a nice performance."

Charlie Bishop timed his challenge to perfection on the heavily-backed Night In Vegas to win the Weatherbys £300,000 2-Y-O Stakes.

Dorigo cut out the early pace alongside Satellite Of Love, with the Eve Johnson Houghton-trained Night In Vegas handily placed in midfield.

Satellite Of Love was the first to go for home but Night In Vegas, whose owners Kennet Valley Syndicates won this race last year with Calendar Girl, was always travelling smoothly in behind.

The 5-6 favourite was shaken up as they entered the final furlong and hit the front with a 100 yards to go and was pushed out to win by half a length.

The winner was fresh from victory in a similar contest at Newmarket, and Johnson Houghton said: "As I said to the owners after last time he won, this is jam now, but it's lovely jam to get!

"It's a nice jam sandwich, but there's plenty more to come."

Night In Vegas was fifth in the Coventry and third in the Vintage Stakes earlier in the season.

However, Johnson Houghton is keen to continue to "go for the money" instead of stepping back up to Group-race company this autumn.

"It's really hard as a three-year-old to win big money, so you've got to win it this year, and then you can go and have fun in black-type races or whatever and try to be clever, but let's just go for the money," she added.

"He's in the Redcar race (Two Year Old Trophy) and he's also in the seven-furlong Tattersalls October Auction Stakes, it just depends whether we go back to six furlongs or go up to seven, and then I think we'll probably end up at Ascot for the conditions race on Champions Day.

"It's been a great year. Last year we hit the £1m barrier with the help of Zavateri and this year we've got some really good horses across the board.

"This horse has definitely been a money-spinner and I'm so lucky to be training him for a great bunch of owners."

Osborne quick off the mark with Speed Of Sound

Saffie Osborne made the perfect start to a big few days on Town Moor by steering Speed Of Sound to a runaway success in the British Stallion Studs 'Carrie Red' EBF Fillies' Nursery Handicap.

It emerged earlier this week Osborne would get a shot at Classic glory on Saturday after being booked to partner the Joseph O'Brien-trained Highwayman in the 250th Betfred St Leger.

Following a third-place finish behind Sun Goddess in a valuable sales race at York last month, the Richard Spencer-trained Speed Of Sound was the 7-4 favourite for the St Leger Festival's curtain-raiser and she dominated from the front, coming home a length and three-quarters clear of the chasing pack.

Osborne said: "It was like riding a piece of work! She's a really lovely filly and very straightforward. I didn't want to make the running but she jumped so quick and was very professional.

"I was able to set pretty even fractions and every time I asked her for a bit more she found it. I've always really liked her, it's just taken a while for the penny to drop.

"Looking at her she's going to be a far nicer filly next year - she's big, strong and robust and I see no reason why she won't stay seven furlongs well."

Spencer added: "The ground at York was too soft for her, but she still ran with credit. Hopefully we can enjoy today and make a plan for the rest of the year.

"We'll see what the handicapper does. There's a handicap at Newmarket, or we may have to go into stakes races, which I think she's capable of doing."

articles.title: Leger Festival: Musical Times 6/1 for 1000 Guineas after May Hill Stakes romp at Doncaster
articles.summary: Musical Times as short as 6/1 for the 1000 Guineas next year after powering to victory in the May Hill Stakes on day one of the Leger Festival at Doncaster; Newmarket's Fillies' Mile the next target for Charlie Appleby's star
articles.body:
Winner of her first two races at Newmarket and Yarmouth, she had not done anything to suggest she was about to blow a Group Two field wide apart.

Travelling strongly in the hands of William Buick, the Charlie Appleby-trained 7-4 favourite shot clear over a furlong out and the race was over.

The daughter of Lope De Vega pulled a yawning seven-and-a-half lengths clear clear of Scommessa Sicura, who was only a neck behind the winner on her debut, in second.

Appleby said: "Delighted. Coming into the race I wouldn't say I was trying to sit on the fence, but she shows so much natural pace at home, I thought 'I hope she stays'. She should stay on pedigree but everything at home has been very zippy and we saw that through the race today.

"She's handled everything and the race was faultless, wasn't it? There was a nice pace on, she travelled into it, travelled up to leaders well and most importantly she accelerated, which is what you always like to see.

"We'll head to the Fillies' Mile, which was always our pencil plan since Yarmouth really."

Paddy Power initially cut Musical Times to 12-1 from 25s for next year's 1000 Guineas, but that did not last long and neither did 8-1, with the firm eventually forced to make her their 6-1 favourite.

"She's handled that slightly slower ground today but she's a neat filly, so if it came up quick at Newmarket in the autumn or in the spring it wouldn't worry me," the trainer added.

"I don't see why she shouldn't be a Guineas filly. We won this a couple of years ago with Desert Flower, who went on to win the Guineas. Funnily enough I see this filly as more of a Guineas filly than Desert Flower, who was a big and scopey and unfortunately didn't quite win the Oaks."

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Doncaster Cup can go to Ballydoyle for first time since 2008
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle reveals her thoughts on the feature races at Doncaster on Friday including the Group Two Doncaster Cup and Flying Childers Stakes
articles.body:
First Cup win since 2008 beckons for Ballydoyle

With question marks hanging over star attraction Caballo De Mar in the Betfred Howard Wright Doncaster Cup Stakes (3.00) at Doncaster on Friday, Aidan O'Brien looks set to take the honours for the first time in 18 years.

The master of Ballydoyle hasn't won the marathon since Honolulu galloped to victory in 2008 - 12 months after Septimus delivered his only previous win in the historic race. However, I expect Queenstown to set the record straight under Ryan Moore following his reappearance win in a Group Three at The Curragh last month.

The six-year-old needs to build on that to avenge a defeat by Caballo De Mar in last autumn's Prix du Cadran but I believe this gelded son of the great Galileo can pull it off with conditions very much to his liking in this Group Two.

There's no questioning the record of George Scott's likely favourite who has a brace of Group Ones on his CV, but he needs to bounce back from two baffling runs in the Gold Cup and the Lonsdale Cup at York last month when he emptied quickly.

Hannon filly set standard in Flying Childers

While the Doncaster Cup is all about stamina, the Group Two Carlsberg Danish Pilsner Flying Childers Stakes (2.25) over five-furlongs showcases raw speed and Richard Hannon's Pershaada has that in abundance.

My old guv'nor has a good record at this meeting and has found a great opportunity for Middleham Park Racing's daughter of Persian Force to win her second Group race of the season. She was electric in the Group Three Molecomb Stakes at the Goodwood Festival when she eased away from a good field including the re-opposing subsequent Listed winner and market rival Sale Shark .

It didn't work out for Pershaada against the older, more battle-hardened sprinters in the Nunthorpe at York, but she sets the standard back against her own generation with the excellent Sean Levey in charge.

I do think Aidan O'Brien's Carry The Flag is a little overlooked, however, after setting strong fractions in the Group One Prix Morny in Deauville last time. Beaten only two lengths in soft ground, he promises to be a handful back over the minimum distance.

I was most impressed by Forgotten Fire's debut win in a Salisbury novice so don't be surprised to see the Andrew Balding-trained filly take the step up in class in her stride in the Listed Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (1.15) on Friday.

Jeff Smith's beautiful home-bred looked a stakes filly in the making when showing a great attitude to slam her rivals over six furlongs and can find the necessary improvement over this longer trip. She's impeccably bred, being a half-sister to Group winners See The Fire and Venetian Prince and is out of Jeff's wonderful Juddmonte International winner Arabian Queen.

I can see why Godolphin's Nabati will be popular among punters as he steps up in grade. His only defeat was a narrow one when he pushed Arapaho Gold all the way in the Listed Rose Bowl at Newbury before Michael Dods' colt won the Gimcrack.

Charlie Appleby's son of Night Of Thunder could be anything at this stage, as his entry in the Group One Middle Park suggests, but I have a feeling Forbidden Fire will set the Town Moor turf alight.

The British Stallion Studs EBF Premier Fillies' Handicap (3.35) on Friday looks ultra-competitive but the standout for me is Ralph Beckett's Nochebuena .

A novice winner over course and distance back in June, she only just failed to hold on in a strong fillies' race at Ascot the following month in a race that has been franked by the winner Hoseki. That was an encouraging handicap debut so a 4lbs rise in the rankings may not be enough to prevent her from taking this prize.

A live alternative is Marco Botti's Golden Muse - a filly I won on at Wolverhampton back in the early spring. It's still early days for her as a turf performer but she did run with promise over a shorter trip at this track earlier in the year.

Newly retired Joe can lead home the legends

The weighing room stars of yesteryear will be so excited to be taking part in the Betfred Leger Legends Classified Stakes (1.50) at Doncaster on Friday. The anticipation of getting back out on the track will be a buzz for them all but I've got a feeling the recently retired Joe Fanning will be the toast of Town Moor.

Joe, who brought an amazing career to a close only this summer, rides Joe Parr's Wield who finished his race off strongly over a mile at Southwell last time. If he can replicate that on turf, he can get off the mark at the eighth attempt.

Sammy Joe Bell has won this race a remarkable three times, so I expect her to go well on another All-Weather performer, the Michael Herrington-trained Anthropologist .

This race has really caught public imagination since its inception in 2010 and has raised well over £1m for the Injured Jockeys' Fund. It's a huge credit to everyone involved, from the jockeys who so sportingly take part to those who work tirelessly behind the scenes.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft .

articles.title: Doncaster tips: Amelia Earhart fancied for St Leger upset at Doncaster
articles.summary: Ahead of the 250th instalment of the world's oldest Classic; Kate Tracey, Declan Rix and Sam Boswell discussed their top tips for the St Leger Stakes; Watch the full episode of Weekend Winners on the At The Races YouTube channel
articles.body:
The team paid particular attention to the feature Betfred St Leger Stakes - which goes off at 3.35pm on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Enceladus currently heads the market for Joseph O'Brien, with the Ballydoyle duo of Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard also in situ. Last year's winning rider Tom Marquand gets aboard Amelia Earhart, while Saffie Osborne rides Highwayman.

"I'm against Christmas Day with Enceladus . He was my ante-post selection, mainly because we knew he was going to go to Doncaster after Goodwood. He's just got this lovely, progressive staying profile rather than having already shown his hand in Classics. He's three from three in 2026, having won his maiden at Cork and the King George VI Stakes at Royal Ascot, before stepping up into Group 3 - winning the Gordon Stakes at Goodwood over just shy of a mile and a half.

His Royal Ascot form has worked out really well, which is important because you could have initially dismissed him as simply being a well-handicapped horse, winning off a mark of 89. The Gordon Stakes demonstrated he belongs in pattern company, and he finished off his race really strongly. He's by Sea The Stars and everything about his progression since being stepped up in trip suggests stamina rather than speed is increasingly becoming his strength.

The step up to a mile and six and a half furlongs in the St Leger is ideal. Comparisons have been drawn between him and Galileo Chrome, who of course won this race for Joseph O'Brien in 2020. Christmas Day - I just think with that Derby form it was a win because of the frailties of his opposition that day and the conditions.

"I'm a Christmas Day backer. Has the favourite really got form to warrant being shorter than Christmas Day? In my book, I'm not so sure. I can see the angle for Enceladus - the progressive nature - and you do get horses who can do that in this race but I wouldn't be shocked if they flip-flop in the betting come the day and I think there will be some support for Christmas Day.

"I'm viewing the York run as that was a stepping stone towards this - we've seen that done in the past. If it rains like it did at Epsom, I have no concerns. He handled the ground that day. I do take the point that you don't know what to make of that Derby still. The Irish Derby second behind Benvenuto Cellini was a fair enough effort and I think this is a two-horse race, given I've lost the faith with Pierre Bonnard throughout the season. I like the horse that has [already] ticked the box on the big day."

"My head is saying this is a pretty average renewal of the Leger and I'm not sure the two Ballydoyle horses are going to take massive steps forward for the trip. Enceladus I really like but I do wonder: why have they put the cheekpieces on? He's a horse who has looked raw and behind the bridle, so maybe that's it but going up in trip, surely you don't want to light him up? Although, he does look the strongest stayer of the market leaders.

"I can't believe I've come around to Amelia Earhart . With her sex allowance factored in, I just think she's interesting. I'm not sure she's going to be in love with winning but on my own figures she's steadily been getting better. She went off favourite for an Oaks having looked very good in the Cheshire Oaks and she's just disappointed. Maybe she thrives at this time of year and not on rattling summer ground, she may get back to her best?

"They've been messing around with headgear. The blinkers have been on, the hood has been on - everything's off now. So they've clearly seen something [and feel] they can eke out improvement. She's a full sister to Cleveland, who won a Chester Cup. Surely going up in trip, of all the Ballydoyle horses she will thrive most - and if she does, she doesn't have loads to find. I'm going to back her in a top three finish at 11/2.

articles.title: Doncaster Cup: George Scott's Caballo De Mar bounces back to form in Town Moor Group 2
articles.summary: Caballo De Mar bounced back from disappointment at York with a decisive victory in the Doncaster Cup; Also on the card, Final Objective got up in the final strides to deny Crownbreaker in the Flying Childers Stakes
articles.body:
Questions had been raised over whether the five-year-old still had the stomach for the fight after coming home last in the Gold Cup and stopping quickly before finishing fourth in the Lonsdale Cup at York.

But after taking up the running a furlong from home on Town Moor under Oisín Murphy, the George Scott-trained stayer proved his doubters wrong, pulling away from Beylerbeyi to land odds of 5-6 favourite by a length and a quarter.

The race had been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven.

Scott is now looking forward to seeing his charge defend his title in the Prix du Cadran on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp.

He said: "We needed to see that from him today if we wanted to go back to Paris with him, as he's two from two there - we just have to hope Scandinavia doesn't turn up there. If he doesn't then he's going to be a player.

"He loves Longchamp, he loves the tempo of the races and two-mile-four is right up his street.

"I thought he was value for a bit more today, he had to commit earlier than he wanted."

The Doncaster Cup was been robbed of its likely favourite after Queenstown was pulled out and there was also drama beforehand when the Emmet Mullins-trained Winday gave trouble at the start. Having worked himself up into a sweat, he failed to the fire in the race itself, finishing a tailed off last of seven.

But on this occasion Caballo De Mar was as good as gold, much to the delight of his trainer.

"His last two races have been in a Gold Cup against two of the best stayers we've seen, and he was third until the furlong pole, and last time at York they went a hell of a gallop and he was in the thick of it the whole way. York is a funny track too, they can misfire and he did," Scott continued.

"Today was a much more of an even set up for him, so I think it's more down to circumstance than anything.

"This horse has been amazing for us for two years - he's had two bad runs, so what - some horses go off the boil for a year before coming back but we got him back within three weeks.

"I said to Sheikh Nasser (owner) this morning, he's a world class athlete and you can train in the gym all you like but if you come out in the afternoon in the heat of battle, that is when you see true colours.

"In the paddock I knew he was on it and Oisin said straight away 'he's here'.

"Victorious Racing put an awful lot of trust in me so it is a relief he's won today. I know that if it goes wrong they have got my back."

Final Objective gets up to land thrilling Flying Childers

Gimcrack runner-up Final Objective came out on top in a thrilling climax to the Carlsberg Danish Pilsner Flying Childers Stakes.

Hamad Al Jehani's juvenile has steadily improved with racing this season, most recently going down by three-quarters of a length to Arapaho Gold at York last month.

Dropping back to five furlongs for the first time, the gelded son of Sioux Nation was a 9-4 favourite in the hands of James Doyle, who produced his mount with a perfectly-timed challenge to get up in the shadows of the post.

Crownbreaker finished a neck second, with Flann Sunna and long-time leader Fast Track close up in third and fourth. In The Black was unfortunate not to do better than fifth after encountering trouble in running before clipping heels and almost coming down passing the line.

Doyle said: "He's a testament to Hamad and his team because he has not been an easy conveyance whatsoever.

"Faleh [Bughenaim], our Qatari jockey, has done a brilliant job with him because he rides him every day so he has to suffer on a daily basis while I only ride him now and again so I have to thank him.

"He was a bit wayward again late on but that is just his nature, he's a bit tricky.

"I was just trying to hang on to their coattails because I was a little bit outpaced early. He's got decent form at six and this was his first time back at five. It wasn't a problem as he's got more than enough speed.

"I thought he was going to win the Gimcrack but when he got out he hung his chance away and I thought he was going to do a similar thing today. He's not easy but he's more straightforward than he used to be."

Forbidden Fire holds off Rock Montreal to win Flying Scotsman

Forbidden Fire resisted the late surge of Rock Montreal to claim top honours in the Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes.

Nine runners went to post for the Listed opener on day two of Doncaster's St Leger Festival and the market was dominated by two Godolphin-owned colts, with Charlie Appleby's dual winner Nabati the even-money favourite ahead of Roger Varian's impressive Yarmouth scorer Rock Montreal at 5-2.

Forbidden Fire, one of only two fillies in the field, was third best in the market at 9-2 off the back of a dominant debut victory at Salisbury, but showed the boys the way home under Murphy.

A daughter of No Nay Never out of owner-breeder Jeff Smith's top-class racemare Arabian Queen, Andrew Balding's filly travelled strongly and had most of her rivals in trouble a furlong out, with Rock Montreal one of the first under pressure at the rear of the field.

However, the latter began to find his stride against the near side rail late on and only missed out on victory by a head, with Nabati beaten into third.

articles.title: Spanish GP: George Russell reveals fears over tyre wear at new Madring track in Madrid for Sunday's race
articles.summary: George Russell says there are concerns over tyres due to the high-speed nature of the Madring and the lack of straights; watch Spanish GP Qualifying from the all-new Madring circuit live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm on Saturday
articles.body:
The high-speed corners at the new track in Madrid are putting a lot of energy into the tyres, particularly the banked 'La Monumental' Turn 12 where the drivers carry huge speed on a 13.5-degree baking.

Russell topped first practice and his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli was fastest in second practice with Saturday's qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1, set to be crucial given the expected difficulty of overtaking in the race.

"There's a big question mark over the tyre degradation. In FP1 with the tyre degradation we all had, we thought a six-stop race would be the fastest way!" half-joked Russell.

"I'm sure tyre degradation will be better on Sunday but with the big long La Monumental, it really hurts the tyres and that will be a challenge for everyone."

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord confirmed the tyre temperatures on the hot Madrid circuit and the lack of straights could create problems for the teams in the race.

"You could see some unusual tyre effects because they are running so hot and you have a lot of cornering sequences without a real chance for the tyres to have a breather," he said.

"It's corner after corner after corner. How the tyres cope with that will be decisive. Even though it's a smooth surface and tyre wear may not be as high as we expect, we may see some other thermal effects that the computers beforehand might expect you to make."

Ferrari to 'shift focus' after practice learnings

Ferrari were Mercedes' closest challengers on Friday as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were both within two tenths of pace-setter Antonelli in second practice.

Leclerc, who is yet to claim a pole position this year, says he's "looking forward to try and do something good in qualifying".

"It's been a very interesting day. A completely new track for everyone and it's very challenging. I think Qualifying will be an exciting one," he said.

"Lots of work ahead of us to try to improve the car for tomorrow but the day went well. We went through our programme and maximised the amount of laps we could do, which was one of the main targets."

Both Ferrari drivers struggled into the downhill braking zone of Turn 17, locking up several times, which team principal Frederic Vasseur suggested was down to the ever-changing conditions.

He also hinted Ferrari focused too much on long run pace and need to find time over one lap as track position will be crucial in the race.

"The long stint was as expected. It's mega difficult to overtake. It means that the positions on track at the start will be crucial," said Vasseur.

"It means also that we have to change a little bit the focus. For sure, it's better to have good pace for the race, but the position in qualifying will be it. Overall it was a decent Friday."

articles.title: Spanish GP: Lewis Hamilton crashes as Kimi Antonelli tops final practice from Charles Leclerc in Madrid
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton crashes in final practice at the Spanish Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli tops the session; watch Spanish GP Qualifying from the all-new Madring circuit live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm on Saturday, and the race at 2pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Just 20 minutes into the session, Hamilton was on course to set a very quick lap until he outbraked himself at the last corner and hit the barriers head-on, albeit at a relatively slow speed.

He reversed out of the barriers but the front wing had dislodged itself and got stuck under the front right tyre, so Ferrari urged Hamilton to stop the car.

But the seven-time world champion wanted to limp back to the pit lane so he did not lose crucial running for qualifying later on at 3pm (build-up from 2.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1 , before eventually coming to a halt in the middle sector.

Sky Sports F1 's Anthony Davidson feels Hamilton was wrong to drive for such a long time with a damaged car.

"Any young driver that is watching this right now, you don't do that. You just don't do that. That's what you could have tried to do [get back to the pits] but that rule is there for a reason," he said.

"If it [the front wing] went under the car completely and jacked your front wheels up and there were marshals on the track... you've got to think of all these scenarios."

The crash caused a 45-minute red flag as the marshals repaired the barriers, with the clock being stopped with 15 minutes remaining so the drivers could get more laps around the new Madring.

Antonelli, who leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points over Mercedes team-mate George Russell, emerged on top with a blistering 1:32.797 to beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by 0.166s.

McLaren showed promise with Oscar Piastri in third and Lando Norris in fourth - the latter missed almost all of second practice on Friday.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fifth and Russell only sixth but it looks like pole position could be anyone's given the drivers are getting faster with every lap and the track is evolving.

Haas' Oliver Bearman proved how difficult the Madring is with a big crash in the high-speed Turn 11, leaving his team with a race to get his car fixed for qualifying.

articles.title: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff fumes at 'couch warriors' questioning team's treatment of George Russell in title battle with Kimi Antonelli
articles.summary: George Russell was beaten by his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli in the Italian Grand Prix after the pair were put on different strategies; watch the Spanish Grand Prix from the all-new Madring circuit live on Sky Sports F1 at 2pm on Sunday, with build-up from 12.30pm
articles.body:
Russell was narrowly leading the race from his team-mate Kimi Antonelli when Mercedes took a decision to pit the Italian under a virtual safety car.

The call ultimately benefitted Antonelli as he used his fresh tyres to pull off a stunning victory having started from 19th on the grid, which increased Russell's deficit to the Italian at the top of the standings to 66 points.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of qualifying at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix, Wolff reiterated his belief that the fact Antonelli was running on a medium tyre and Russell a hard tyre completely justified the decision.

"It's absolutely the right thing we did," Wolff said. "He (Russell) was on the hard. It was predicted to be a one-stop as the better strategy.

"The medium was a compromise; we had to put the medium on Kimi because he started on the hard.

"There is just no way, and obviously there are some couch warriors that will drop their comments after having watched some other material online… saying that he was penalised is complete bull****."

Russell started the season as the clear title favourite but has been outperformed by Antonelli, with the 20-year-old having dramatically exceeded expectations during just his second F1 campaign.

The Brit backed Mercedes' decision following the race in Monza, insisting that Antonelli deserved credit for his performance.

Wolff admitted that "harsh calls" are required to win championships but insisted that there is no "hidden agenda or favouritism" with his team.

"That's been part of our role in the last 12 years, to manage both sides of the garage well," Wolff said. "Because if you are in a title fight, one is always going to be disappointed after a race and the other one is going to be happy.

"I think as long as you're transparent and there is no hidden agenda or favouritism, then it's the best to manage it.

"But it doesn't mean that we are not making some harsh calls. We are having stern talks on a Sunday morning - what are the various situations we are facing? Behind some pressure from another team, and one of our drivers behind the other one and it's too slow, we're going to invert the cars when it's needed.

"But it's a decision that you need to take sometimes, in either direction by the way, whoever is in front. The decisions you need to take in order to win a championship, but it's always going to be balanced."

'We could have looked like idiots, like Ferrari'

Ferrari shared the headlines with Antonelli following the Italian Grand Prix after a first-lap incident between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, which saw the former push his team-mate into the gravel, resulting in the loss of several places.

Wolff said that the clash made Ferrari look "like idiots" but wanted to avoid being overly critical of his rivals given Antonelli and Russell came close to also leaving Mercedes red-faced.

The Austrian said: "I can express my opinion now and say it's not on to push your team-mate off in Turn 2, but three or four laps from the end, we had some scary moments between the two of them that we didn't expect in that way because George had a tyre that was shot, and Kimi was a second quicker.

"Did we expect them to fight like they did, which could have ended up with a car in the gravel?

"We could have quickly looked like idiots as well, like the Ferraris looked, eventually, so it's a fine margin."

articles.title: Betfred St Leger: Saffie Osborne becomes first woman to win a British Classic as Highwayman lands Doncaster feature
articles.summary: Highwayman led home a 1-2 for trainer Joseph O'Brien in the 250 Betfred St Leger at Doncaster, beating Enceladus, with Amelia Earhart in third; Saffie Osborne the first female jockey to win any one of the British Classic races
articles.body:
Handed the plum spare ride on the improving Vinnie Roe Stakes winner as just reward for a fine season, the eye was drawn to the 24-year-old who was moving stylishly into contention as the runners entered the long Doncaster straight.

With the Ballydoyle contingent seemingly beaten off as Osborne sent her mount on with a furlong to run, the only danger appeared Billy Loughnane and 5-2 second-favourite Enceladus.

However, Highwayman (11-) was not for reeling in under an inspired Osborne who entered the record books on the 250th anniversary of the world's oldest Classic.

Osborne told ITV Racing: "I don't think I've ever been speechless in my life and I didn't have this on the bingo card for this week.

"I didn't have a ride in the race on Monday morning, let alone one with a chance, and I can't thank so many people enough. Firstly Joseph and his team for putting their faith in me, it won't change Joseph's life, but it will change mine.

"My agent Tony Hind, I would be nowhere without him and I know it's cliched but my mum, dad and whole family. This means the absolute world and as I crossed the line I was in shock. I just can't believe it and it just doesn't feel real.

"I was more forward than I anticipated, but he was travelling so well into it, I couldn't believe it."

Delighted winning owner John Neocleous said: "The horse did it so easy didn't he. I wish I could say more about it, but I'm still in shock!

"This horse was 250-1 in a maiden (at Naas in June), that was the wrong distance of course, but it's amazing how far he has come. We should not be surprised, though, because Joseph keeps on making history.

"You don't know where this horse will end up, but he did win pretty easily today.

"We're going to Australia, I think, but Joseph will make the decisions, he's in charge.

"We won the Galway Plate a month ago with King Alexander so it's been a hell of a summer but this is a different level completely."

Regarding his history-making jockey he said: "Saffie is amazing, I'm sure she's in shock as well.

"Joseph came up with the idea, but he called me first and I was extremely happy to have her, she's an up-and-coming jockey, she knows how to ride a finish and I thought if she rode a good finish maybe we'd be placed. But she won comprehensively so I'm very happy.

"I said to Saffie, 'let's go and make and history', but I didn't really believe it!"

O'Brien watched the race from Leopardstown where he told Racing TV: "The two of them are two really nice, progressive stayers.

"It's a special race and he was impressive I thought.

"He was a slow learner and mentally he was immature, but when he got rolling he improved hand over fist.

"Enceladus is a huge big horse and he'll make a smashing four-year-old."

articles.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Big fan of Forty Years On in Sceptre Stakes on final day of Doncaster's Leger Festival
articles.summary: The Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05) features on the final day of the Leger Festival at Doncaster, all live on Sky Sports Racing; Scandinavia stars in Irish St Leger at The Curragh
articles.body:
Scott filly can make winning Stakes debut

I've made no secret of my admiration for FORTY YEARS ON who can make an instant impact in Pattern company when she contests the feature race at Doncaster on Sunday, the Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05).

George Scott, who won Friday's Doncaster Cup with Caballo De Mar, has found a great opportunity for this most progressive daughter of Mayson who was much too good for her rivals in a valuable handicap at Goodwood last month.

She enjoys ease underfoot and can win for the sixth time in eight starts at the possible expense of Shadwell's Touleen , who brings solid Group One form to the race after her luckless run in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot.

She did look a bit awkward in the Valiant Stakes last time so the cheekpieces may just sharpen her focus, while Planet Seeker looks over-priced on the strength of her York form and her creditable fourth in the Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Longer trip ideal for Bailey gelding in Mallard

It's hard to fault SAY WHAT YOU SEE in the Betfred Mallard Handicap (3.40) on Sunday following a string of rock-solid races for his trainer Liam Bailey this year.

He built on a near miss at Southwell with an eye-catching run at York's Ebor Festival, staying on from a long way back to finish a closing third over 12 furlongs and should appreciate this longer trip.

There's probably a nice race in Godolphin's Valedictory who was a little one-paced over two miles at York last time, having looked the real deal earlier in the season with back-to-back wins at Goodwood and Newmarket. He has something to prove off his current mark, however.

I like George Boughey's lightly raced ASUKA in the Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (1.55) on Sunday's Doncaster card.

Dropping back to six furlongs on such a big galloping track shouldn't be an issue for the Night Of Thunder gelding who confirmed himself in top form over further at Chester last time when a poor draw and an interrupted run put paid to his chances.

George has a strong hand in the race with stable mate Oliver Show also bringing some strong form to the table. His run behind subsequent winner Inspired at Goodwood last time reads well and the first-time visor is an interesting angle.

Easier surface a positive for course winner

I'm looking forward to seeing LANGSTONE back on an easier surface in the Betfred City Of Doncaster Handicap (2.30) on Sunday.

Clive Cox's three-year-old broke his maiden over course and distance in the spring before following up on the All-Weather but didn't enjoy the fast ground in the Britannia at Royal Ascot. He hasn't been seen in public since so he arrives on Town Moor much fresher than his rivals and remains well treated off a slightly reduced mark of 92.

Zooming should also appreciate a more sympathetic surface for the first time since winning her maiden at Newmarket last autumn. She has been highly tried this year and drops into handicap company for the first time off what looks a workable mark of 94.

I can't wait to see how SUN GODDESS performs back at Group One level in the Moyglare Stud Stakes (2.50) at The Curragh on Sunday following her demolition job in a valuable sales race at York last month.

Aidan O'Brien's filly had it all to do after running into trouble on The Knavesmire, but her class prevailed in the end as she ran out a most impressive six-length winner. This is much tougher, of course, as she tackles seven furlongs for the first time on a stiffer track, but I'm confident the Phoenix Stakes winner is up to the task.

Green Empress travelled well when getting off the mark in the Group Two Debutante Stakes over course and distance last month, beating the re-opposing Alpha , Ibelieveicanfly and Dancing Destiny and looks the main danger.

Sandals ready to take a big step forward

The way Starlust hit the line behind US raider Bacio in the Nunthorpe Stakes at York tells me he can run another massive race in the BAR 1 Betting Flying Five Stakes (3.25) at The Curragh.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old came out of retirement following a fruitless spell at stud and looks to have found the form that won him the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint two years ago.

TIME FOR SANDALS' last two runs have been solid, and I like the way she flashed home in the Nunthorpe after repeatedly finding trouble mid-race. If things fall her way, she could be the one they all have to beat with Kieran Shoemark in the saddle.

Sequoia can post a giant run in National

Juddmonte colt Monogram looked a class act when scoring over course and distance for Joseph O'Brien and can take the step up to Group One company in his stride in the Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (4.00).

One thing he does lack, however, is experience which could give GIANT SEQUOIA the advantage. Aidan O'Brien's first string won the Group Two Futurity Stakes here last time and is clearly a colt of huge potential.

On the evidence of that run, the son of the great Frankel is still open to enough improvement to make his presence felt at the very highest level so gets my vote in a mouthwatering renewal.

Brilliant Scandinavia set for fifth Group One

With a seven-race unbeaten streak to his name, I can't wait to see the brilliant SCANDINAVIA enhance his reputation in the Comer Group International Irish St Leger (4.35) on Sunday.

Aidan O'Brien's Gold Cup winner steps back to one mile and six furlongs which shouldn't be a problem on such a stiff track, and he can justify short odds in his quest for a fifth victory at the highest level.

Stable companion Jan Brueghel , who, like Scandinavia is a Doncaster St Leger winner, is the obvious danger. He looked as good as ever when winning this season's Coronation Cup and won't mind this greater test of stamina.

articles.title: Spanish GP: F1 drivers braced for race-day mystery on Madring debut with tyre and overtaking uncertainties
articles.summary: Lando Norris heads front row from Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in behind on row two, with many unknowns for the new Madring circuit's maiden race day; watch the Spanish Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 2pm on Sunday, with build-up from 12.30pm
articles.body:
The wall-lined circuit in Madrid has proved a big challenge for drivers so far on its inaugural weekend, while Friday's practice running showed up tyre degradation difficulties on long heavier-fuel runs.

The grid's leading drivers are braced for those challenges to continue into a 57-lap race for which McLaren's Lando Norris starts on pole position ahead of Mercedes' championship-leading Kimi Antonelli.

Mercedes' Russell, who qualified sixth after a disappointing Q3, told Sky Sports F1 : "I think tyre degradation will define it one way or another.

"There will either be no degradation and it will be a procession, or really high degradation and it will be pretty chaotic."

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who qualified fourth having initially held provisional pole after the first flying laps of Q3, is also expecting tyre management to play a central role.

"We all came into the weekend thinking there would not be much degradation and the tyres would last long but it turns out there was a lot of degradation [on Friday]," said Hamilton.

"I'm sure that will improve as the car gets grippier, but I have no idea what to expect."

And championship leader Antonelli, who was pipped to pole position by a sensational final lap by Norris, predicted: "Probably it's going to be grandmother driving in the first 10 laps, but let's see.

"We saw in the long run how steep the degradation can be, especially if you push too early. We will try to see in the moment.

"Maybe we go into the race and the degradation is going to be much lower."

Why Norris is on the 'backfoot' despite pole

It seems track position could be critical, so, in theory, Norris is in the best position as he starts on pole ahead of Antonelli, Verstappen and Hamilton.

But, the McLaren driver missed almost all of second practice on Friday due to a gearbox issue and has not completed any meaningful long running as a consequence.

"I have to do my homework tonight. I'm on the backfoot from a high fuel perspective. I've not done any," Norris told Sky Sports F1 .

"I need to use the data we have from Oscar and see what uses I can have, looking at onboard videos and data from everyone.

"Not an ideal situation but I gave myself the best chance and we will prepare the best way possible. Luckily it's not the best track to overtake on, so we will focus on a good start, good lap one and see what we can do."

In Friday's practice sessions, the tyre degradation was extremely high due to the successive high-speed corners, including the big banked 'La Monumental' Turn 12 where the tyres experience high loads.

"Everyone found out there was a lot of graining on the tyres," said McLaren team principal Andrea Stella.

"I'm not sure everyone has clear ideas as to what strategies we have ahead of us, so it will be entertaining."

The pace between the front-runners should be close, so the race is likely going to come down to tyre degradation, which will dictate how much overtaking there is.

Norris is in the best position, as he can control the pace, but if overtaking is possible, he cannot afford to drive too slowly to save his tyres. But that's the big question mark, is there enough room to overtake?

"The only thing you can do is try to put pressure on the car in front, trying to make them make a mistake or make them deg a bit more, and then you try to play with strategy," said Antonelli.

"But, especially when you have a very similar pace, it is difficult to make a move."

The awkward turn five chicane is expected to be the best overtaking spot, but Verstappen feels the curvature of the track means it will even be difficult to attack into that particular corner.

"In some places, in the braking zones, they need to learn that you should never have to steer while braking. You need to be able to combine under braking because otherwise it doesn't allow any kind of overtaking," said the Red Bull driver.

"For sure, in terms of track design, I think it can be better. I also think driver input on track design in the future could help a lot. I know they'll always come back to you and say, 'Yeah, but the space,' but that's BS. There's always a way to create an overtaking opportunity around a track."

articles.title: Spanish GP: Kimi Antonelli wins F1's first Madring race to increase title lead after Lando Norris misfortune
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli increased his championship lead to a commanding 81 points with his eighth race win of the year; Lando Norris appeared to have race under control before untimely Virtual Safety Car lost him the lead; Max Verstappen second, while Lewis Hamilton suffered first DNF of his season
articles.body:
McLaren's Norris had looked in control of the race after converting his superb pole position into a comfortable early race lead but the battle for victory turned on a lap-14 Virtual Safety Car when Aston Martin's Lance Stroll stopped in a run-off area.

With a VSC offering the field the chance of a so-called 'cheap' pit stop, McLaren were unable to pit Norris immediately as the Briton had just passed the pit-lane entry road.

But the following Antonelli and Verstappen had not, allowing Mercedes and Red Bull to pit their drivers respectively while Norris was running to a controlled reduced speed on track while marshals moved Stroll's car.

McLaren did pit Norris at the end of the next lap but, by then, the VSC had ended, meaning the field was back up to racing speed, with that misfortune then compounded by a slow seven-second service at the tyre change.

Norris rejoined in fifth place and, underlining his prodigious pace, eventually finished on second-placed Verstappen's tail in third but was tantalisingly unable to find a way past the Red Bull through the closing laps.

With George Russell finishing only fifth in the second Mercedes behind a long-running Ferrari of Charles Leclerc, Antonelli's title lead grows to a season-high 81 points with a scheduled nine races remaining.

Antonelli said: "I think today it's good to win but it doesn't feel as good because I think Lando today deserved the win but overall, we take it."

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton is now 101 points back and all but out of contention after he suffered his first race retirement of the season after his car ran into terminal brake issues inside seven laps.

Liam Lawson was sixth for Red Bull with Alpine's Franco Colapinto seventh ahead of Oscar Piastri in the second McLaren. Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad was ninth with Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in 10th.

'We were too quick, that's all it was' - How luckless Norris' speed led to his misfortune

Before the VSC was initiated on lap 14, Norris appeared to be shaping up for a repeat of his dominant recent wins at the Hungaroring and Zandvoort as he raced into a lead of six seconds over Mercedes' Antonelli.

The reigning world champion had come under attack from the championship leader at the race start but Antonelli was soon on the back foot when he cut the first chicane under braking. It put the Italian into the lead on the exit, but he clearly had to give the place back to Norris, which he swiftly did.

Antonelli attempted to go around the outside of the McLaren again into the next chicane at turns five-six but had to bail out of it once more, again cutting across the run-off. But when he let Norris through for a second time, he was unable to prevent Verstappen following through too at turn seven and so dropped to third.

But Antonelli was soon back ahead of Verstappen after Red Bull told their driver to drop back both behind the Italian and Hamilton having jumped the latter back at turn one by running off track. Verstappen disputed that interpretation of events over team radio, saying he had no choice but to run wide, but heeded the order.

Norris, meanwhile, had quickly set about building a lead and was already 3.2 ahead of Antonelli when Verstappen dropped back on lap four.

The Briton was five seconds clear by lap nine and his lead had grown the lead by a further second by the time the VSC was initiated. In the end, that supreme speed proved to be Norris' undoing, as he was already beyond the pit entry so could not pit immediately whereas his fortunate pursuers were not and so could.

Speaking on team radio after the race, Norris said: "Just take it on the chin. We were too quick, that's all. Very unlucky today guys, we should have won."

McLaren chief executive Zak Brown concurred, telling Sky Sports F1 : "That was our race by 20 or 25 seconds.

"He was dominant, he was gone. Managing, great tyre wear - a league of his own."

Is there now any stopping Antonelli in the title chase?

With Norris returning to the track after his delayed and then slow stop initially behind Russell in fifth place before the Mercedes pitted for a second time, a victory for Antonelli appeared almost inevitable despite there still being 40 laps to go.

However, the Italian did not actually lead the race until the end of lap 48 as Ferrari kept Leclerc out on hard tyres in the hope of their being another Virtual or full Safety Car intervention. There was not.

As Leclerc's pace eventually started to drop, Antonelli caught up with the Ferrari but, with passing opportunities severely limited around the Madring lap, the Mercedes had to follow behind. That allowed Verstappen and Norris, easily the fastest car on the track, to close right in on the top two before Leclerc finally pitted.

In the end, once in clear air, Antonelli pulled away from Verstappen by four seconds over the closing laps, with Norris unable to find a way past the Red Bull, for his second win in eight days after his stunning back-to-front triumph on home soil at Monza.

Asked afterwards whether he was now starting to think about the championship, the 20-year-old Antonelli cautioned: "That's exactly what I don't want to do.

"I want to keep pushing race by race, keep delivering and keep enjoying it all the way and try to do my best every race and we will see where we end up at the end of the year."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver calls for rule changes to Formula 1 Virtual Safety Car rules after losing out on win to Kimi Antonelli
articles.summary: Lando Norris says the timing of the Virtual Safety Car at the Spanish Grand Prix was "unfair" as it cost him victory to Kimi Antonelli in Madrid; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.

However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of their [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1 .

"A race should be won by the guy who can put in the best performance. Maybe you take a risk by running long in a stint and maybe you get a Safety Car and things can help because you know that's one of the big factors.

"But for everyone to get a VSC pit stop and for me to not, it's just.. unfair. But it's happened in the past. Others have won from it, I've probably won from it in the past. I just don't think many people have lost a race win over it. It's frustrating. I don't feel that's the way you should lose."

Race-winner Antonelli stated he "felt bad" for Norris and the McLaren driver feels everyone should have the opportunity to pit, should a VSC be called.

"We have spoke about it in the past in drivers' briefings saying they [race control] should leave it out for at least a lap, so it's equal for everyone," he continued.

"I was the only one that lost out and I lost out on about 20 seconds of race time and that's not how it should be."

McLaren chief executive Zak Brown told Sky Sports F1 : "They [the VSCs] were cruel today twice!

"Lando was gone, the team did a great job and the VSC came out a couple of seconds after we went by and went away a couple of seconds before we could pit.

"Nothing we could have done. Great to hear Lando's radio message to 'shrug it off'. That was our race by 20 or 25 seconds. He was dominant, he was gone. Managing, great tyre wear - a league of his own."

Why did Norris not stay out and pit later?

McLaren had the option to not pit Norris straight away so he could potentially build a gap to his rivals, particularly as Charles Leclerc stayed out and was holding up Antonelli.

However, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says Norris' medium tyres were too worn and he would not have enough pace to pull away.

"We considered staying out but you have to accept the fact that now you're on relatively used medium tyres and the people behind you will be on new hards, so you're never going to open a gap on people on new hards," said Stella.

"Therefore, we kind of needed to accept that was what we should have done. And the fact that it was incredibly unfortunate. Sometimes we talk about being unlucky. I think at times that being unlucky is used for too many applications, but in this case, it's almost a mathematical definition of being unlucky."

Virtual Safety Cars were introduced to Formula 1 in 2015 following Jules Bianchi's tragic accident at the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix.

An indirect consequence of them is drivers drive to a delta which sees them go 30 to 40 per cent slower compared to green flag conditions.

The same rules initially apply when there's a full Safety Car, before the field gets bunched up, but it means a sporting advantage can be gained by pitting.

"It is racing and it's happened, so I can't really complain about it. I can be upset about it, but I can't really complain about it," said Norris.

"I think there are things, because we have spoken about it in the past several times, about how it can be at least covered for one lap or everyone has the opportunity to do the pit stops, or you just block the pit entry and no one can box apart from if you have a puncture or something.

"So, I think there are a few things you could do to make it more simple and more fair for everyone, but that's a bigger discussion. This is not something I can just ask for."

Norris' maiden win at the 2024 Miami Grand Prix came with the help of a Safety Car which enabled him to have a cheaper pit stop against Max Verstappen.

But he pointed out that a rule change would require all drivers to come together to agree on new regulations.

"I think we would all want, but there's a lot more to it. Depending on if it's raining and there's a VSC and you're on slicks, does it mean you can box or not? So it's a complicated subject," he said.

"But I think as a collection of drivers, if we all talk about it, I think everyone wants the same thing, and that's just fairness for everyone. Of course I'm complaining about it today, [but] I could benefit from it next week, next time out, and I could win because of it.

"I have to take it on the chin, but I just hope it doesn't happen to anyone again because it's just not how you should lose a race."

articles.title: F1 drivers, team bosses hopeful over Madring track changes for overtaking after new venue's first Spanish GP
articles.summary: Lando Norris believes there are "easy changes and maybe some more tricky" for year two to improve racing at the Madring; Toto Wolff confident organisers open to ideas; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The new home of the Spanish Grand Prix held its inaugural event over the weekend around the semi-permanent, wall-lined Madring circuit

While the 3.36-mile layout was praised for the challenge it posed on a fast qualifying lap, drivers had raised concerns ahead of the race about a likely lack of overtaking opportunities - something which largely played out in the race.

Lando Norris, who claimed the inaugural pole position and would likely have won the Grand Prix too but for an untimely Virtual Safety Car, believes "there are some obvious changes they should make" to make it a "great race track" to go with the challenge it provided drivers in qualifying.

Offering a blunt assessment on some immediate revisions he would like to see, the McLaren driver said: "They should get rid of [Turns] 18, 19. Useless. Just have more of a straight into a hairpin.

"Like, I don't know how someone looks at this design and goes, 'Mint'. Yeah, I think there's a lot of opportunity.

"Like I said yesterday, I think they can make it into a track that's good for racing, and I'm excited to come back here next year if they can make these changes because I think it's a track that is good fun to drive and it can be a great race track."

Race winner Kimi Antonelli added: "I think there are some corners that need to be changed to create more overtaking opportunities because right now, yes, it's nice over one lap, but for sure in the race, you know, you're just stuck behind [other cars]."

Williams' Carlos Sainz, one of two Spanish drivers on the grid and who is also an ambassador of the Grand Prix, wrote on X: " The track is great. There needs to be some work done to create better passing, but it's been a great race overall, especially for a first year."

'They are totally open-minded about next year' - Wolff sure organisers will make tweaks

The inaugural race weekend at the Madring, which winds round Madrid's IFEMA exhibition centre and is located close to the Spanish capital's international airport, drew a sold-out crowd of 352,618.

Toto Wolff said he was impressed with the event as a whole and revealed organisers were already talking to the FIA, F1's governing body, about what could be improved regarding the track for next year.

"I think for the first [event], it's probably one of the best, or maybe the best that I've seen so far," said the Mercedes team principal.

"It's a temporary circuit. They've built something that is challenging for the drivers - a mini Macau or a mini Monaco - and the location is good.

"We are thinking about how much more we can do next year in terms of little events here, or presentations, because we have the space and that's very rare in Formula 1.

"So I would say congratulations for a first.

"And then it's the tricky bit, doing a track that is spectacular also for the drivers and then building it in a way that there is lots of overtaking.

"I had a discussion yesterday with the CEO of the circuit and they are totally open-minded about next year and said 'we've had the discussions with the FIA. What is it we should do? How is it that we should lay the track out when it comes to overtaking?' There is a constant discussion.

"And I think that they are on it and understand 'can we tweak it a little bit here or there?' Honestly, I feel like if you try to find a hair in the soup, then you always find one. But being here for the first time, I'm very impressed."

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies was similarly effusive about the facility and also expressed hope that track improvements would be explored and introduced.

"It was an incredible event, that's my opinion," said Mekies.

"Incredible event, incredible venue setup. Massive paddock, massive garage area. I think it was a fantastic track in terms of being a driver's track, all sort of corner speed and all of that in between the walls.

"I think the only shortfall is the overtaking opportunity. I'm guessing it is stuff that can be addressed even [with] the space that we have around the track layout.

"I'm not a track designer but I would think that there would be certainly a common desire to want to improve probably the only aspect, or the main aspect, that remains behind here which is the overtaking opportunity."

Norris offered further suggested alterations to the existing layout.

"It's great in qualifying, but, you know, straight line from 17 straight to 20, have a much wider entry like Austin Turn 1 or Turn 10 in Austin, big hairpin," he said.

"You know, you'll create much better opportunities for everyone and you'll be able to enjoy the race.

"So yeah, there are some simple changes and maybe some trickier ones, like Turn 5, 6, 7. It's hard to know exactly what's the best thing.

"The fact you have to turn and brake basically defeats the whole object of racing. So, they can do some simple changes, I think, easy changes and maybe some more tricky, but I hope they do it because then it should be more exciting for everyone."

Speaking after qualifying on Saturday, Red Bull's Max Verstappen had said: "In terms of track design, I think it can be better.

"I think also input from drivers in the future on track design can also help a lot. I know they will always come back to you and say, 'Yeah, but the space,' but that's BS. There's always a way to find an overtaking opportunity around a track.

"But overall, the event itself is very cool. I mean, yes, they've done a great job.

"Also how quick, I think, they made the track available, the information that was shared for the simulator. So, from that sense, I think, yeah, it was very good. But in terms of, if you want to have better racing, overtaking, I think there can be a few corners that can be changed."
