articles.title: Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle delves into the talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix, assessing F1's newest venue and where it can be improved, the debate around the rules that cost Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli's ever-growing world championship lead
articles.body:
It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.

The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

However, under a virtual or actual safety car, due to the speeds and geography of the layout, there was a chunky 12-second advantage in pitting under the safety car while rivals are travelling much more slowly. And that decided who would win the race.

With so little circuit knowledge, especially for Lando Norris who had missed virtually a full practice session with car gremlins, and for others who had had sizeable shunts along the way, this meant that all three available tyre compounds were represented on the grid.

On the front row, pole sitter Norris, after a sensational qualifying lap, and fellow front-row sitter Kimi Antonelli had medium compounds. Max Verstappen was on soft compound tyres, like Lewis Hamilton. Others like Charles Leclerc's Ferrari and George Russell's Mercedes were on the hard compound tyres.

And that's how they set off. Norris got away reasonably well and aggressively covered off Antonelli. The young Italian would fail to slow enough, and bypass both of the two early chicanes, hitting the throttle hard through the run-off areas.

This meant he would clearly have to give back to Norris the lead he now had, but Verstappen read this very well, and using his speed, guile, and soft compound tyres, he would not let Antonelli simply hand the place back to Norris without helping himself to second place.

However, in the melee early after the start, Verstappen too had a straight run through a chicane, in his view to avoid a shunt with Hamilton.

In the view of the stewards however he had gained an unfair advantage and, much to Max's chagrin, his team told him, before the stewards did, to hand the place to Lewis which by now necessarily included Antonelli too.

It probably cost Max a victory in the end.

How the Virtual Safety Car turned the race Antonelli's way

Antonelli is definitely getting the rub of the green in this phase of the season, although it must be said that his speed and consistency have enabled him to make sure he doesn't waste these golden opportunities, and on lap 14 he would be handed another.

Norris had been flying out front, looking very assured. But when Lance Stroll lost his Aston Martin under braking and became marooned down one of the few and short run-off areas, it looked reasonably certain that there would be a virtual safety car to recover that.

Norris was fast approaching the pit-lane entry, the team didn't want to pit him on simply the chance of a safety car rather than the certainty, given how hard it was to overtake even significantly slower traffic if they didn't pit.

Just as the race director gave the VSC order, Norris had passed the pit entry. But his lead was over four seconds and, critically, Mercedes did have time to pit Antonelli. If only Lando hadn't been in such great form…

Ferrari kept Leclerc out on his hard tyres, the relatively early safety car hurting his strategy. But clearing away stricken cars had been rather slow all event and might, just might, Norris be able to complete another lap at safety car speed and still get a cheap pit stop in?

Not at all. It went green and full racing speed when he was two corners from the pit-lane entry, and he then had to navigate the whole pit lane whist his main rivals were flat out. And to cap it all, McLaren delivered him a seven-second pit stop rather than the usual two seconds.

Undeterred, Lando set about catching up to Verstappen and Antonelli in fine fashion.

Leclerc would impressively lead until he pitted on lap 48 to park his tired hard tyres. If that sounds long, a very unimpressed Pierre Gasly was left out on track by his Alpine team for 55 of the 57 laps.

This all left Antonelli in the lead, but with Verstappen pushing hard as Norris was catching him, the three leaders were close together in the final stages.

But there was no way past, and having led his 13th straight F1 race, Antonelli would now lead the championship by 81 points from his team-mate Russell. It's the fifth consecutive race where the 20-year-old Italian has extended his points lead.

Mercedes power units also won their 251st race in F1 history, tieing with Ferrari. Impressive numbers all round.

Russell in the other Merc was mighty fast too and would catch Leclerc but had to be content with following him home in fifth place, being a relative outlier on a two-stop strategy by pitting on laps 14 and 28.

It simply won't fall into place for George, he's not catching any breaks this season so far.

Sadly, Hamilton's Ferrari had brake issues in the opening laps and he would retire for the first time since Brazil last season. This meant Liam Lawson, standing in for the injured Isack Hadjar, grabbed eight more points in sixth place for Red Bull to go with Verstappen's excellent 18 for second place, in a car which wasn't second fastest.

The VSC rule debate and expectations of 2027 Madring change

Antonelli and Verstappen were both immediately magnanimous post-race when declaring it Norris' victory without the unfortunate virtual safety car timing. Should a driver lose a race because another driver has made a mistake or had a car failure?

What goes around comes around in the course of a season and even a career, but it felt rather like a robbery on Sunday.

Some racing categories temporarily close the pit lane except for emergency repairs (or emergency refuelling if they have that), but that can all get a bit confusing and congested too in the pit lane and is still not equal for everyone.

One solution might be to ensure that if a virtual safety is deployed, then it must stay in place for at least a full lap of all the runners to keep it fairer. Although, of course, that costs green flag full-speed racing time, which is what people want to see in the grandstands and on their devices.

By next year I hope and expect that the Madring will have some track layout changes to improve overtaking, a more condensed and practical set up behind the scenes, and better signage for all. It has all the ingredients to make a credible contribution to the F1 season.

articles.title: George Russell: Mercedes driver's losses to Kimi Antonelli will feel 'painful' says Nico Rosberg as driver backed for breakthrough
articles.summary: George Russell fell 81 points behind Kimi Antonelli at the Madring; Russell conceded that "realistically I'm not in the fight for the drivers'" after the race; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Russell's hopes of becoming world champion for the first time this year are increasingly slim with in-form Mercedes team-mate Antonelli opening an 81-point lead over him at the top of the standings.

Since winning March's season-opening Australian Grand Prix, pre-season title favourite Russell has only twice finished ahead of Antonelli in the last 10 races they have both completed with the Briton seeing the young Italian take his seventh and eighth wins of the season across the Monza-Madrid double header.

Rosberg was asked after Sunday's race, in which Russell finished fifth, on Sky Sports F1 about his experience of rebounding to win his world title in 2016 after being soundly beaten to the crown by Mercedes team-mate Hamilton the year before.

"I was driven a lot by the pain," recalled Rosberg.

"Subjectively, it was painful to keep losing against Lewis and that just drove an insane motivation.

"George will be in a similar situation. He will be so damn motivated at the moment to try and find improvements.

"He'll be working so hard because I know George doesn't give up and he's hating the situation of getting beaten over and over by Kimi.

"He'll be working super hard but it's a bit of a difficult one because it's hard to understand where the pace has gone for him."

Russell has been Mercedes' top-scoring driver in three of his previous four seasons at the team, twice in three years against Hamilton (2022 and 2024) and once alongside a rookie Antonelli (2025), but he requires a major turnaround for that to be the case again this year with nine scheduled races left.

Rosberg believes the diligent Russell will keep working away to find a breakthrough with the W17 car, although says it is inevitable that the 28-year-old will be questioning himself too.

"I'm very impressed with George's approach because he's really a perfectionist and he tries to cover every aspect of his human performance," added the Sky Sports F1 pundit.

"I know he's doing everything he can, and I admire that.

"But, all the more, it's tough for him because he doesn't understand himself. He's always been fast; he's always been at least level with his team-mate and suddenly it's gone away from him there.

"It's really painful because you start to doubt yourself. It doesn't matter how confident you are, it then comes [to questioning] 'am I not good enough? Was I better in the past and I'm just doing something wrong now?' It's really difficult."

'Realistically I'm not in the fight' - Russell all-but rules out drivers' title win

Fresh from being beaten to victory by Antonelli the weekend before at Monza despite his team-mate starting a penalised 19th on the grid to fall 66 points off the pace, Russell conceded going into the Spanish Grand Prix weekend that he would "need some luck" to realise his title dreams this year.

That deficit grew to a season-high 81 points in a disappointing weekend for him at the Madring, which was compromised by a difficult Q3 in qualifying and then an early Virtual Safety Car in the race. That result led to Russell all but ruling himself out of contention on Sunday evening.

Assessing his approach for the forthcoming races, starting with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on September 24-26, Russell told F1 : "Just keep pushing along. It has been a more positive couple of races even though the result was far from great today.

"But it's kind of story of the season. I just need to focus on the performance, keep trying to help the team.

"We're obviously in a great place to win the constructors', realistically I'm not in the fight for the drivers', and that just allows me just to focus on race-by-race and trying to focus on getting some good results."

'We just have to unlock it' - Wolff backing 'top driver' Russell to find breakthrough

His Mercedes team remain convinced Russell will rediscover his best form.

Asked what Russell was fighting hardest at the moment, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said: "I don't know, because you can see the pace he had towards the end when he was catching Leclerc. He was fastest out on track.

"But after the tyre changes, the pace wasn't there.

"I just don't know where it is and we have to analyse it, because clearly it's in him, it's in the car, and we just have to unlock it."

But Wolff has no doubt that, even if this title eludes him, Russell will "recover" and be a factor in many more world championship fights.

"When it comes to George, you can have good races, bad races, good years and bad years, but we're talking about the driver that has won everything that he could have potentially won before," added Wolff, who signed Russell to Mercedes' junior programme in 2017.

"Every single karting championship, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in his rookie year, went into the Williams.

"I mean, we're talking about a top driver. We need to find out what is it for him to be able to unleash that potential.

"And of course, there's the psychological side. If you have a run like him this year, you're taking a beating.

"But the great ones, they recover. And George has all he needs to fight for championships. Even if that one has maybe sailed, there will be more."

articles.title: Fernando Alonso: What's the latest on Aston Martin driver's future as he weighs up retirement or new contract to stay in F1 in 2027?
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso's future became a major talking point in Madrid after FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said he wants to help engine manufacturer Honda; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Alonso has been frustrated with Formula 1's 2026 regulations and the performance of his Aston Martin-Honda car, having scored points just twice this season.

The 45-year-old, whose current contract at Aston Martin expires at the end of this season, suggested how he feels about the power unit tweaks for next year, which will see the electric output reduced from its current near 50 per cent to 42 per cent, will dictate his decision.

"It's a matter of understanding what the rules from next year will have an impact or not on the racing and on the driving side of things," said Alonso last Thursday at the Spanish Grand Prix.

"The current cars, as I said many times, are not the best cars to drive and to enjoy. But next year there is a step in the right direction, hopefully.

"At the same time, I need to think what is the best programme for next year and sit with the team. Behind the wheel or in another role, where I will be helping the most, that will be the most important thing to decide together."

Are FIA set to help Honda to keep Alonso in F1?

A day after Alonso's comments, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem appeared to reveal he wants to accelerate Honda's engine development so they can catch up.

"There is no way we can allow Fernando to leave - Alonso, a great champion - just because of the circumstances. That's not the way to leave the stage," said Ben Sulayem.

"He has to be successful and then he leaves whenever he wants, not because he was forced to leave because of the performance.

"I share the issues. The car is not performing. I met with Lawrence [Stroll] on Thursday and I'm going to do the changes and will talk to him to make him, try to make him, change his mind. It's not acceptable."

The comments could be seen as a personal intervention by Ben Sulayem but Sky Sports F1 understands the FIA president wants to work with the Power Unit Advisory Committee, which features all five engine manufactures, to work together to help Honda.

One option could be changing the ADUO (Additional Development Upgrades Opportunities) rules to not only be about the ICE (Internal Combustion Engine) power.

Honda have already used one of two engine upgrade opportunities this year, have at least another two for 2027 and were given an extra £14m of development budget.

Ben Sulayem added: "I will be speaking to him. I said to him, I saw him very sad, and I said, 'Fernando, I understand, it's not acceptable that you are coming to your own country and now after two times a world champion and you are at the last'.

"We did something earlier, in May, legally for the team towards the engine to go and improve, and then I said to him, 'I am not going to tell you what we are going to do. Please tell me what you want because you are the driver and come and tell me what do you want us to do to improve these results.'

"Suddenly you see everything change, then I get a call and I had a meeting [with Stroll]. We are here to support."

Red Bull were deemed to have the best engine earlier this year by the FIA, although most people in the paddock feel Mercedes are the benchmark engine manufacturer.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies are open to changes in order for Honda can catch up.

"The ADUO in that case was designed as a catch-up mechanism and that formula was unlocked for Honda, and they need more," said Wolff.

"And the conversation that the president had with Alonso is fair enough. We want to have all of these top constructors in the sport. We want them to be competitive and successful.

"And regulations are regulations to be for the best of the sport and sometimes maybe they need an adjustment, so fair enough conversation."

Mekies added: "As much as we cannot agree all the time, as a sport we try to keep a fairly open look at the regulations.

"You may recall that actually there was a first change in the ADUO regulations done earlier this year precisely in order to help those who were much behind, compared to what was initially voted. All the teams voted that, we voted in favour of that for the benefit of the sport.

"As I said, we cannot agree on everything but certainly as stakeholders of the sport if there is a situation that needs to be fixed or needs to be supported, we normally find solutions. And I'm sure that we will at some stage sit down and discuss the future of the ADUO regulations. The shortfalls, we know some of them, and I'm sure there is a few of those to address later on."

So is Alonso going to stay or retire from F1?

It is hard to judge whether Alonso's initial comments were sparked by a push to get rule changes which will aid Aston Martin and Honda, or he's genuinely unhappy with the current F1 cars.

Perhaps it is a combination of both and it should not be forgotten Alonso made his F1 debut in 2001 - an era with roaring normally aspirated V10 engines - a contrast to now.

There will certainly be an element of Aston Martin not being competitive too which is part of Alonso's thinking and that brings us to how long does the Spaniard want to race in F1 for, if he can't compete at the front?

Alonso will be 46 years old next summer and the last driver to race in F1 at that age was Graham Hill in 1975. The Spaniard became a father earlier this year and hinted he still has other motorsport ambitions after admitting a return to the World Endurance Championship and the Le Mans 24 Hours is an option.

Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack said at the weekend in Madrid: "We were always clear the team wants to continue. We have made it clear all through, but we need to respect what Fernando's thoughts are.

"We need to respect the time he wants to take. And, as I said before, we're confident we can reach a good solution for everybody. And now it's about waiting. He needs to make up his mind and then we move on."

Most of the 2027 F1 grid is locked in after Max Verstappen signed a new Red Bull contract and Williams duo Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon committed to staying for next year.

Only the second Red Bull seat alongside Verstappen, Racing Bulls, Haas and Audi are yet to confirm their line-ups so Aston Martin won't have the option to sign a perceived top driver to replace Alonso, should he retire.

Krack said: "I will also not speak about any Plan B. We very much hope that Fernando will continue. He's very important for our team. He's very important for Formula 1. He's very important for the whole sport and motorsport in general.

"It would be a pity to not have him anymore. And because that would be so dramatic, I do not even want to talk about it or think about it."

articles.title: F1 2027 calendar announced with Bahrain to host season-opener and increase in Sprint weekends in 24-race schedule
articles.summary: Bahrain to host 2027 Formula 1 season-opener as Portugal and Turkey return to the schedule from next year, plus an increase in Sprint weekends; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.

Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

Australia reverts to the third round of the season in early April and will also host a Sprint, as will the next race in Japan before China rounds off a triple-header.

Miami retains its slot in the first weekend of May before Sprint rounds in Canada and, for the first time, Monaco, with F1 highlighting fans are "set to enjoy two thrilling qualifying sessions" around the streets of Monte Carlo.

The returning Portuguese Grand Prix slots into mid-June and is followed by a Sprint weekend at the British Grand Prix on July 2-4, with Austria moving to after Silverstone.

Back-to-back weekends in Belgium and Hungary will take the F1 circus to the summer break.

A sprint round at Monza in early September will be the first event back after five weeks off, a week longer than usual, with the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid a week later.

Azerbaijan, Turkey and Singapore form part of a triple-header before the usual Americas triple-header in Austin, Mexico and Brazil, which is a Sprint weekend.

Las Vegas will host the only Saturday race of 2027, although it will be Sunday morning in the UK, then two Sprint weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi on December 10-12 conclude the season.

"The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 president Stefano Domenicali.

"We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Turkey to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to 10 events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special.

"Formula 1 continues to go from strength-to-strength, attracting new audiences around the globe. Week after week, the world's greatest drivers will battle on some of the most challenging tracks in motorsport, supported by F1's outstanding teams, world-class manufacturers, and global partners. Together, they create a spectacle unlike anything else in sport. As we continue this remarkable journey of growth, I want to thank our fans around the world as their passion drives everything we do."

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added: "The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport.

"With 24 Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Turkey, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

articles.title: F1 2027 calendar: Monaco staging one of 10 Sprints and other talking points from race schedule reveal for next season
articles.summary: Assessing the increase in Sprint races for the 2027 Formula 1 season, including Monaco, plus other changes to the sport's racing schedule; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
But the schedule features a number of points of intrigue including an increase in Sprints, headlined by the addition of Monaco, the continued presence of the sport's usual Middle Eastern rounds, and the return of two popular tracks...

As reported in July , Formula 1 is increasing the number of Sprint weekends on the calendar for 2027.

The final number of Sprints has been confirmed as 10, four more than the six which have featured in each of the past four seasons.

The alternative format, which was first introduced in 2021 and features an additional qualifying session to set the grid for a short-form 100km race, has led to increase in global television audiences, which F1 says are 12 per cent higher than on non-Sprint weekends which feature three practice sessions.

The 10 venues for 2027 are split evenly between tracks that have staged Sprints previously - Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Interlagos and Qatar's Lusail - and newcomers to the format in Sakhir, Albert Park, Suzuka, Monaco and Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina Circuit.

The current Sprint format, which features points for the top-eight finishers, is thought set to remain the same for 2027.

Why Monaco is staging a first-ever Sprint

Certainly, many of the early headlines and debate around the 2027 calendar has centred on the fact Monaco has unexpectedly been included as one the 10 Sprint venues.

Not only has the Principality never hosted a Sprint before, its main 78-lap Grand Prix is already not known for overtaking around its narrow, twisty wall-lined circuit with the race often proving processional in dry conditions.

It is regularly Qualifying - and the flat-out challenge of threading an F1 car between the barriers - that proves the most jaw-dropping aspect of the Monaco weekend. F1 has pointed out that the addition of the Sprint means there will now be two such grid-setting sessions in 2027

It can also be argued that having only one practice session, rather than the usual three, offers the chance for more unpredictability in the pecking order given drivers will only have one practice session to build rhythm and confidence, a crucial element of a successful Monaco weekend.

"Traditionally Sprints have been held at tracks where it is easy to overtake. Clearly that's not the case at Monaco," said Sky Sports' Craig Slater.

"But the big bonus here we'll have two red-hot qualifying sessions. That's what that track is all about and the drivers will have the ultimate test on two occasions that weekend."

For the first time next year, the season will both start and finish with a Sprint event.

Bahrain opens the season with the format on March 12-14 while Abu Dhabi will close it on December 10-12.

The season-opening Sprint will certainly present a different challenge for teams and drivers given they will have just one practice session that weekend to prepare for the campaign's first competitive session, Sprint Qualifying, on the Friday evening.

However, pre-season testing at the same Sakhir circuit (February 24-27) will run to four rather than three days - one more day than is usually the case outside of years featuring big rule changes - meaning they will at least be familiar with the track with the new 2027 cars.

Still, the season-opening Sprint represents a new challenge and could offer some early-season surprises in the pecking order for one, or both, grids if teams are not on top of their cars and set-ups.

The fact that the season will finish with back-to-back Sprint events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi inevitably raises the possibility of the world title being decided in a Saturday race should the fight go down to the final rounds.

There is already precedent for this from Qatar 2023 when Max Verstappen clinched his third world title in the Sprint.

Middle East races scheduled as F1 waits on final 2026 decisions

The sport's four Middle Eastern races all feature on the 2027 season, bookending the 24-race campaign.

That also remains the case for 2026's final two scheduled races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi with just over two months to go until the sport is due to head there.

The conflict in the Middle East has already seen this year's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix cancelled and the Bahrain Grand Prix moved to Malaysia on October 4, having originally been scheduled for April at its own Sakhir track a week before Jeddah.

F1's intention and planning remains for 2026's concluding two rounds to go ahead as scheduled. Although Stefano Domenicali had previously indicated that there was a mid-September timeframe on making a final decision on whether the events could take place, there is thought to be no hard deadline as such with officials able to wait for longer before making a final call.

Italy's Imola circuit is understood to be the contingency to close the current season in December should the Middle Eastern rounds not be able to take place.

The early-season 2027 dates in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are not scheduled for another five months, giving F1 and the FIA plenty of time to continue monitoring the latest situation.

Formula 1's calendar first increased to a record 24 grands prix in 2024 and that number is again scheduled for next year.

Next year's calendar features no absolutely-new venues, but the sport will return to Portugal and Turkey for the first time since the popular European venues were called up to help out during the Covid-affected 2020 and 2021 seasons.

They replace the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which starts a rotation with the Belgian GP and next returns in 2028, and Dutch Grand Prix, whose deal has ended.

Portugal's Portimao circuit takes over Barcelona's June slot, while Turkey returns at the start of October as part of a slightly rejigged run of races after F1's summer break, which will stretch to five weeks in 2027.

The season will finish on December 12, one week later than this year and the joint-latest since 2020.

articles.title: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull driver's injury recovery going to plan as team provide update on next steps ahead of Azerbaijan GP decision
articles.summary: Red Bull's Isack Hadjar has missed three races since the summer break with an injured wrist; team to assess whether Hadjar is ready to return ahead of Baku; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Hadjar has missed the last three races after sustaining a wrist injury during routine training ahead of the sport's return to action from its summer break. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson has stood in for him.

Speaking after last Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix, Mekies said Hadjar's recovery was going to plan, with a simulator session planned to help assess his readiness for any return to action in Baku.

"There is nothing wrong with Isack's recovery. I think we have learned that it's fundamentally a normal time for the sort of injuries he has," said Mekies

"So, we will continue with the same approach and what we have.

"We will evaluate the situation in a week's time.

"We have a full week, a bit more than a full week, to evaluate situations, to see how he feels and then to put him on the simulator, to expose him to real-life constraints.

"And if he feels close to 100 per cent, we go for it. If he feels the recovery is not completed, we will stick to our approach to put his recovery first.

"What we don't want to do is, by having an early return, compromise his long-term capacity to come back to 100 per cent."

The Azerbaijan GP, held on a street circuit in Baku, starts a day earlier than normal with practice taking place this coming Wednesday ahead of a Saturday race. It is the first round of a triple header with races in Malaysia and Singapore following on the subsequent two weekends.

Red Bull pleased with Lawson's 'very good' stand-in performances

Lawson has stepped up from sister Racing Bulls to cover for Hadjar, with the New Zealander returning to a seat he briefly held in an ill-fated two-race stint at the start of last season. Yuki Tsunoda has been driving for Racing Bulls.

Lawson has twice qualified eighth and scored points at both Zandvoort and Madrid, where he was sixth.

"I think he's done a very good job," said Mekies.

"I think we all know how difficult it is to jump to a different team, to a different car, and I think he has done that to the best of what could have been our expectations.

"He has taken some very important points [in Madrid] with the P6. He did the same in Zandvoort, and in Monza he would have done something similar without the contact with Nico [Hulkenberg] and the damage.

"So, I think he did a very good job. Again, very different pictures compared to the first races of 2025 when he was in the team, so we are thankful and happy with that."

Lawson has rebuilt his form and confidence at Racing Bulls over the past year and was already enjoying a consistent points-scoring season before his unexpected temporary senior Red Bull return.

"I think he has continued to grow as a driver," added Mekies, who has worked with Lawson at both Red Bull teams. "He's very calm in the car; he's very focused.

"He's certainly making... I don't know if he makes an effort or not [to do it], but he's certainly managed to keep things simple in the way he tracks with the team and in the way he tackles his own performance and the car performance.

"So, he's focused on the essentials; he tries to get the basics right, and it's working for him. Of course, with more time in the car, you can then get to another degree of finesse, maybe.

"But I think that, of course, is very, very strong."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver reacts to Monaco Sprint news for 2027 season after Formula 1 calendar surprise
articles.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix was named as one of 10 Sprint venues on the 2027 race calendar; Norris says only one practice session will test drivers; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The 24-round 2027 calendar, published on Wednesday, includes 10 Sprint weekends - four more than this season - with Monaco's street circuit to host the alternative format for the first time.

The Principaliy's narrow track is not known for overtaking, where the Sprint format has hitherto tended to be used, but is considered arguably the greatest challenge in the sport for an F1 driver when it comes to qualifying.

Reacting to the news when speaking with Sky Sports F1's Natalie Pinkham alongside golfer Justin Rose during an appearance at the BMW PGA Championship Pro-Am at Wentworth on Wednesday, McLaren's Norris said: "Interesting.

"I guess the main thing is that means you've got FP1, [Sprint] qualifying on Friday - which is the challenge.

"Obviously not a lot happens in a race on Sunday or in the Sprint, but the challenge is just one practice session straight in, which has probably never happened before in Monaco."

Drivers normally have three one-hour practice sessions to build up a rhythm and momentum around the twisty wall-lined track, on which mistakes are usually heavily punished. Set-up and on-track preparation work will now all have to be squeezed into just 60 minutes.

On the new challenge that the Sprint schedule presents, Norris said: "That's more [about] relying on data from this year.

"You don't have as much time to build up to things so you're going to you're probably going have to try and risk a little bit more earlier which is normally when you can see a bit more of a difference between people who can get comfy, try things and be at 99 per cent and not go to 103 and 104 [per cent] because in Monaco when you go to that limit, game over.

"It's more exciting for the fans and the people watching."

Norris won the Monaco Grand Prix from pole position in 2025 during his title-winning year.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton responds to reports he has asked for Ferrari personnel changes ahead of Azerbaijan Grand Prix
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton took to social media on Thursday to "clear up" reports claiming he has asked for personnel changes at Ferrari; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Hamilton has fallen 101 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli with nine rounds to go, having scored just eight points in the last two races.

Ferrari brought an upgraded engine to their home event at the Italian Grand Prix but Hamilton only finished sixth, while Charles Leclerc crashed out, before a brake problem caused Hamilton to suffer his first retirement of the season in Madrid.

This week, reports in the Italian media have stated the seven-time world champion has been pushing team principal Frederic Vasseur to make operational changes, but Hamilton took to Instagram on Thursday to shut down the rumours.

"I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up here. I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward," he wrote.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves. I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

Hamilton called for "rules of engagement" at Ferrari after he was forced wide into the gravel by team-mate Leclerc at the Italian Grand Prix on the opening lap.

The British driver stated "the buck starts with Fred (Vasseur)" before Ferrari held talks with their drivers where Leclerc admitted he was at fault for the incident.

Hopes of a record-breaking eighth world title have diminished since the summer break with Hamilton not scoring a podium in the last five races.

"I think there's no stopping him (Antonelli) and Mercedes this year," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 after Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.

"They've done a phenomenal job and they deserve it."

articles.body:
The first round of a flyaway triple header before trips to Malaysia and Singapore, the Baku race weekend starts a day earlier than normal meaning Practice is on Thursday, Qualifying is on Friday and the Grand Prix is on the Saturday.

Kimi Antonelli leads the world championship by 81 points after consecutive wins in Monza and Madrid and time is running out for his would-be title challengers to put a run together to rival him with a scheduled eight rounds left after Baku.

But, as then-title leader Oscar Piastri found to his cost at last year's race, the wall-lined Baku circuit can certainly bite if you make a mistake with challenges present all round the fast and tricky layout for both qualifying and race day.

The Baku race takes place a day earlier than normal on a Saturday (September 26) as it is the country's Remembrance Day on Sunday September 27.

That means 2026's Grand Prix takes is being held on Saturday, with Qualifying on the Friday and the opening two practice sessions on Thursday.

Azerbaijan is three hours ahead of the UK so the sessions are slightly earlier than they were during the European season, with Qualifying at 1pm and the Grand Prix at midday.

In the country on the Caspian Sea where Europe meets Asia, the Baku City Circuit joined the F1 calendar in 2016. The race ran under the European Grand Prix title in that first year, before taking the country's name from the following season, and is one of the breed of the sport's faster street tracks.

That speed is no more evident than when drivers top 200mph down the 1.4-mile long main straight - the longest of the whole season - with slipstreaming and overtaking opportunities aplenty as cars go up to three abreast. The big Turn One braking zone was the scene of a crash between Red Bull team-mates Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo in 2018.

After two shorter straights connected by classic street circuit-style 90-degree turns, the 3.7-mile track heads into the twister ancient part of the city, including the narrowest piece of track of the whole season. At 7.6 metres between the barriers, the tricky Turn Eight-Nine 'castle' chicane takes F1 cars past what is the city's UNESCO-protected medieval area.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Arapaho Gold can continue unbeaten run for Michael Dods in Newbury's Mill Reef Stakes
articles.summary: Our ambassador Hollie Doyle spotlights the Group Two Mill Reef Stakes on a stellar card at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing; she also reveals her Ayr Gold Cup fancy and provides the latest on her recovery from a broken leg
articles.body:
Dods gelding to strike gold in Mill Reef

Michael Dods has been bullish about his unbeaten gelding Arapaho Gold , who can make it five wins out of five in the Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes (2.12) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

The impressive Gimcrack winner - according to the Darlington trainer the best juvenile he's ever had - boasts by far the best form in the race and proved his liking for this course and distance when he won the Listed Rose Bowl earlier in the season.

Godolphin's Nabati looked most progressive until coming unstuck in the Listed Flying Scotsman Stakes at Doncaster only last week. Charlie Appleby is backing him up quickly with something to prove at this level.

I'm keeping a close eye on the revitalised Breeders' Cup winner Starlust in the Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (1.02) at Newbury.

Ralph Beckett's sprinter, who stole the glory in Del Mar two years ago before an unsuccessful stint at stud, has run two big figures at the top level in the Nunthorpe and the Flying Five in Ireland last weekend so poses a threat to all in this lower grade.

Back on an easier track, he can get his head back in front at the possible expense of Shagraan , who can outrun his odds in the first-time cheekpieces. Clive Cox's gelding was second in this race last year and will enjoy the underfoot conditions.

Roaring Legend proved he retains plenty of ability when going down narrowly to last weekend's Mallard winner Valedictory at Newmarket in the summer and can go one better in the Dubai Duty Free Autumn Cup Handicap (1.37) at Newbury.

Olly Murphy's eight-year-old is a fresh horse - a comment that applies to Alan King's Insanity . I've always liked this gelding who is well handicapped on the pick of his more recent form.

Primo Lara has Ryan Moore up which will attract plenty of market interest but this looks much tougher than the all-weather race he won at Kempton earlier this month.

Richard Hannon holds the key to the Dubai Duty Free Handicap (2.47) at Newbury with the consistent Boyfriend and stable companion Stem .

The former was quite unlucky at Salisbury when things got quite congested but he stayed on well and might have gone closer with a clear run. Compensation way well await.

Stem produced a good run at Sandown last time and has won at Newbury before, while Jane Chapple-Hyam's Balzac posted a much-improved run at Ascot after being gelded and looks another big player.

Binhareer is a stakes horse in the making so I'm expecting big things from him in the Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup (3.40) at Ayr on Saturday.

William Haggas' grey ran a super race in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury in July off an unchanged rating of 103 and my husband Tom Marquand is looking forward to getting back on him in handicap company.

A course and distance winner in easy ground last year, he's on top of my shortlist along with Far Above Dream who went agonisingly close in a hot handicap at York last time. That form was franked when the third Coul Angel bolted up at the Curragh last week.

At a bigger price, I wouldn't rule out Richard Spencer's Run Boy Run , who won the race 12 months ago off a lower rating and could be dangerous in first-time blinkers if he's drawn on the right side in stall 23.

I'd love to see Sam England win the Ladbrokes Ayr Silver Cup Handicap (2.30) with the in-form Trilby who is another strong chance for Tom (Marquand).

He won well at Beverley before staying on nicely at Haydock, hitting the line really hard, and the quicker they go the better for the six-year-old who is on a nice mark despite his five-pound penalty.

Wathnan Racing's Deep Havana also shoulders a penalty but won well at Thirsk off a long lay-off and can improve on that, while Julie Camacho's Havana Blue should play a leading role after winning so impressively at Ascot.

Getting back on simulator my biggest milestone

I'm delighted to report that in the past two weeks I've really turned the corner in my recovery from the broken leg I sustained at Bath in May.

For a while I wasn't seeing the progress I was hoping for which was quite worrying - my knee and ankle just weren't working together - but I'm starting to see good results now which is very satisfying.

The biggest milestone was getting back on the simulator a few weeks ago. Initially I couldn't even get my foot up in the iron but it feels good to be taking such a big step back towards riding again.

Even from the outset I was determined not to let myself lose too much condition, hoping that I would be able to regain fitness faster once I started to increase my rehab, which has been quite exhausting.

I've been doing an hour in the gym every day at Oaksey House in Lambourn, followed by physio sessions and work in the hydro pool. I've also been back on the exercise bike which has been great for boosting my cardio.

I'm definitely ticking every box and seeing the results of my hard work so I'm hoping to be back doing what I love in a matter of weeks, rather than months.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

articles.title: Weekend Winners: Almekarem backed for handicap victory at Newbury on Saturday with Stem also fancied
articles.summary: The Weekend Winners team of Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Declan Rix reconvene to preview an exciting weekend of racing from Newbury - live on Sky Sports Racing - and Ayr; watch the episode in full on the At The Races YouTube channel
articles.body:
Having claimed a 17-runner handicap at Doncaster's St Leger meeting, Almekarem heads the betting (at the time of writing) for Sir Mark Prescott, despite a 5lb hike in the weights from his Town Moor appearance.

Boyfriend is another who has been penalised by the handicapper following positive recent runs, while Balzac looked to have rediscovered his mojo after being gelded when a runner-up at Ascot earlier this month.

Rossa Ryan and Ralph Beckett team up with Gonna Fly, and Jamie Spencer gets on board Stem, who will look to build on a positive third at Sandown the last day.

"I think I know how this race is going to work out, even though there are plenty of runners lining up for this year's renewal. I think you need one that will settle behind this strong pace and I am going to side with Almekarem after he landed a nice handicap at Doncaster last week.

"The horse has got gears, with the family having plenty of progression with triple-digit-rated siblings. He heads the market, but I think he is on a rapid improve and can take the beating on the back of a good performance last week."

"I am with the Richard Hannon-trained Stem , who I think is a little bit forgotten about here. He ran in the competitive Spring Mile at Newbury - where he ran well and the form of that race has worked out throughout the season.

"He's running over 10 furlongs after being ran over eight [and 12] furlongs [so far this season]. I think he has every chance of running his race and at 8/1, I think he's a solid proposition at those odds."

"I'm siding with a winner of the Polish Oaks - which isn't something I say every day - in Merveilleux Lapin for Owen Burrows. She has been largely consistent since joining the yard without winning and I think she's a shade over priced here.

"She bumped into some progressive types at Ascot last time and although the Burrows stable form isn't as good as I was hoping recently, he did have a nice winner the other day at Yarmouth. At 16/1, she will probably be the value play for me."

articles.title: Mill Reef Stakes: Charlie Appleby's Nabati reverses Arapaho Gold form at Newbury
articles.summary: Partnering Nabati, former Kingsclere jockey William Buick won the 2026 instalment of the Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes, which was run in honour of Ian Balding; Also on the card, Jack Nicholls won his first Group prize aboard Miss Yechance
articles.body:
Kingsclere graduate William Buick and Nabati thwarted Andrew Balding's Jolivette in a finish fitting of a race named after Park Stables' most famous resident.

Returning to the track a little over a week after finishing third in the Flying Scotsman Stakes to Balding's Forbidden Fire at Doncaster, Charlie Appleby's youngster this time turned the tables on the Kingsclere team as the 7-4 chance successfully dropped back in trip to six furlongs with the narrowest of short-head verdicts.

Michael Dods' 5-4 favourite and Gimcrack hero Arapaho Gold - who beat Nabati over course and distance in July - also played his part in an excellent finish to the Group Two feature, but the aftermath centred on the Balding family and a winning jockey firmly taken under their wing at the distinguished Hampshire academy.

Buick said: "I was 12 during the first summer holiday I started going to Kingsclere and I have some great memories. When I was watching the videos on the screens before racing of Ian talking about Mill Reef it brings back so many great memories and it's amazing to have had the time there I did. I was so lucky.

"I woke up this morning and thought this lad is running back a bit quick, but it's in honour of Ian Balding so I better do my best as he will be watching.

"I hope he would have been pleased to see us both going at it from the furlong post to the line and he would have nodded and said you both did your best. A dead-heat would have been perfect but it's great to win this race."

Nabati was giving Appleby and Buick back-to-back Mill Reefs after the triumph of Words Of Truth 12 months ago and Buick added: "He was tough there today, we thought we would ride him a bit more forward today but he came out the stalls a bit awkward and ended up where we were.

"I got him in a nice rhythm and I got after him a little bit earlier than planned and he had to fight, which he did.

"At Doncaster the action unfolded away from us and he probably didn't have a hard race as a consequence of that, but it was a great call by Charlie and the horse has repaid him."

Reflecting on the brave effort in defeat from Jolivette in second, Balding said: "I was delighted with the run, she put it all in but just couldn't quite get the job done. She's a lovely filly and it's great to get her Group Two-placed.

"She's a talented filly and goes on any ground and she's a bit of a star.

"I'm very grateful for Newbury and Dubai Duty Free for giving dad the honour of having his name attached to this race and it was almost the perfect result, but at least Will won it and he's a Kingsclere boy."

Miss Yechance a first Group winner for Jack Nicholls

Jack Nicholls continued his fine association with Miss Yechance as the jockey landed the biggest race of his career to date in the Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes.

The 20-year-old had guided the speedy three-year-old to handicap success at York's Ebor meeting and was entrusted with steering Karl Burke's filly once again, making all for a neck success at 12-1 over Clive Cox's Shagraan, whose stablemate Diligent Harry grabbed third from 9-4 favourite Starlust.

It is perhaps fitting the first major triumph of Nicholls' fledgling career has come aboard a sprinter given the exploits of both his father Adrian and late grandfather Dandy over the shorter distances, with the Group Three victory another notable moment in what is becoming a fine season for the apprentice.

Nicholls said: "I rang my dad on the way down and said I think I can be in the first four and if I can do that I would be over the moon and he just said, 'keep a level head kid, don't do anything you normally wouldn't'. I did that and it worked out, so I'm over the moon.

"He was some man for sprinters to be fair to him so hopefully I can follow in his footsteps."

He went on: "It's been the season of dreams really and I've ticked off everything I wanted.

"I said after I won the heritage handicap on her at York I'd love to win a Group race on her and for my first ride in one to be a winner is pretty special.

"I loved that and there is no bigger buzz and especially for the boss, who has been superb to me since the start of my claim. For him to trust me in a Group race is really special. The owners also put a lot of trust into me being a 3lbs claimer, so this is great."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli versus his mind will decide 2026 Formula 1 title race, says Nico Rosberg ahead of Azerbaijan Grand Prix
articles.summary: On the latest episode of Sky Sports F1s The F1 Show, Nico Rosberg discusses what Kimi Antonelli will need to overcome to become world champion; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from this Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
Antonelli is on course to become F1's youngest world champion at 20 years old as he leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 81 points, Ferrari's Lewis Hamiton by 101 points and McLaren's Lando Norris by 106 points.

Just nine rounds remain this year, starting with this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix which will see the race take place on Saturday at 12pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event .

Speaking on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show , Rosberg brought up his own title-winning experience in 2016 where he faced a big mental battle which Antonelli may also need to overcome.

"I know how my head started to play games with me when I was the big favourite," said Rosberg.

"When you're really the big favourite, like he is now, it's like, 'oh my God, this is this is actually mine for the taking. I better not mess this up, I better not make these make stupid mistakes and unnecessary mistakes now because the World Championship is there for the taking'.

"As soon as those kind of thoughts come in, you start to get scared and you really start to get fear that you're going to mess something up completely unnecessarily because it remains that driving an F1 car and being at the front of the pack, of course, is one of the hardest things in the world to do.

"It is so damn difficult to not make mistakes and to be there, qualify time and time again and do good laps and not put it on the wall. It is easy to make mistakes because it's just so damn hard. Then your head starts to go, and it just takes capacity away from your concentration to drive well."

Antonelli has shown no signs of any nerves as he has won the last two races, including an incredible drive from 19th to first at his home event at Monza, then at a new track in Madrid a week later.

In 2016, Rosberg was in a much tighter title fight against Hamilton but was in a position where he did not need to win the last four races and could afford to finish second, with one third.

He continued: "When I was going for my World Championship, the last four races, that's when it really went crazy in my head, and there was no chance in the world for me to do a pole position or to win another race in those last four races because I had like 30 per cent less capacity in my mind to actually drive well.

"Usually, it's like 100 per cent to drive well, and now it was 70 per cent to drive well, and 30 per cent was just absolutely terrified to make some stupid mistake and lose my opportunity to win the Formula 1 World Championship, which is just so extremely big.

"It was a massive dream that also Kimi has been working towards since he's eight years old. So it's 12 years of dedicating his life, which is more than half of his life, towards the dream of maybe being F1 world champion. It's so big.

"That's the big one that we need to keep an eye out. It's really him against his mind now, so we see how that goes, but he's doing incredibly well."

Rosberg: Worst-case scenario if McLaren edge away

Antonelli has largely had the upper hand on team-mate Russell for much of the season, so unless that suddenly changes, his biggest competition could come from Ferrari or McLaren outdeveloping Mercedes.

Norris could have won three of the last four races, had it not been for an untimely virtual safety car last time out in Madrid, so he appears to be Antonelli's biggest threat despite being fourth in the Drivers' Championship.

McLaren have new parts for this weekend's race in Baku, before Mercedes bring a major upgrade package for next week's race in Malaysia.

"The worst-case scenario is if suddenly McLaren starts to edge away, and maybe there's also a Ferrari improvement or something, and Kimi starts to drop back into the pack a little bit more," said Rosberg.

"That again is similar to where I was in my championship year, because I was not driving as well, I started to drop back into the pack in those last four races.

"Even in Mexico in qualifying until the last moment, I was actually only sixth in Q3 until the last moment. In each of those races, I was P3 at some point and not P2, and Max Verstappen was banging into me like every single race.

"If you were to drop back into the pack ever so slightly, again, the risk just comes up more and you start to get more and more panicked about things."
